Rule:
ID: LOL-CAP
Title: Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs
Kind: parametric
Summary: Liability must be capped for both parties at a meaningful amount, with standard carve-outs.
Severity: critical
Category: liability
Position — preferred:
Mutual cap equal to the greater of (a) fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000; mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages; carve-outs (uncapped) for breach of confidentiality, data protection and security obligations, indemnification obligations, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, and infringement of the other party's IP; Customer's payment obligations are not "damages" for cap purposes.

Position — fallback:
Mutual cap of 12 months' fees; carve-outs at least for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct.

Position — walk-away:
Customer's liability uncapped while Vendor's is capped; Vendor cap below 6 months' fees; indemnities inside the cap with no super-cap.

Detection guidance:
Find the limitation-of-liability, exclusion-of-damages and any "aggregate liability" language, including language hidden in warranty or indemnity sections. Determine: does a cap exist; what is the basis (fixed amount, months of fees, fees "paid" vs "paid or payable"); is it mutual or one-sided; which obligations are carved out. Resolve defined terms ("Fees", "Losses", "Claims") — a cap on "Fees" defined as a small set-up fee is illusory. A one-way cap that protects only the Vendor, or language stating the Customer's liability is unlimited, is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Edit the existing sentence(s); do not rewrite the section. Change the basis to 12 months' fees, make the cap mutual, and add one carve-out sentence. If Customer is uncapped, add Customer to the cap. Comment: state the position and that indemnities/confidentiality sit outside the cap.

Model language:
Except for Excluded Claims, each party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (a) the fees paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000. "Excluded Claims" means a party's breach of its confidentiality, data protection or security obligations, its indemnification obligations, its gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud, and its infringement of the other party's intellectual property rights.


Claimed finding status: deviation

Finding rationale:
Caps are mutual and use a 12-month fee basis (Sections 9.1(c)/9.2(c)), and the consequential-damages waiver in Section 10 is mutual with a carve-out for Customer's payment obligations, so the structure meets the fallback shape. However, three points deviate from our preferred position: (i) the monetary floor is only $100,000 (vs. USD 1,000,000) and is measured on charges "paid" rather than "paid or payable"; (ii) there are no carve-outs from the cap for breach of confidentiality/data protection and security obligations, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud or infringement of the other party's IP (only indemnity payments and bodily injury/property damage sit outside the capped bucket); and (iii) Section 9.1(c)(2) excludes IBM's liability entirely for loss of or damage to Customer's records or data, which is a one-sided exclusion of our principal risk in a hosting arrangement. The redline raises the floor to $1,000,000 on both sides, adds "or payable", adds a mutual Excluded Claims provision, and confirms the data-loss exclusion does not cover IBM's own security or confidentiality breaches.

Rule:
ID: INDEMN
Title: Indemnification by Vendor
Kind: missing
Summary: Vendor must indemnify Customer for third-party IP claims and its own misconduct; Customer's indemnity stays narrow.
Severity: critical
Category: indemnity
Position — preferred:
Vendor defends and indemnifies Customer (and affiliates) against third-party claims alleging the services or deliverables infringe IP, arising from Vendor's breach of law, data breach caused by Vendor, or gross negligence/wilful misconduct; standard procedure (notice, control, cooperation); Customer's indemnity limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.

Position — fallback:
Vendor IP indemnity with usual exclusions (Customer modifications, combinations, specifications) and remedies (procure, modify, replace, refund); Vendor indemnity subject to a super-cap of 3× annual fees.

Position — walk-away:
No Vendor IP indemnity at all, or a one-way Customer indemnity for Vendor's services.
Detection guidance:
Locate indemnification / hold harmless / defence language. Deviation if Vendor indemnity is absent, or only Customer indemnifies, or Vendor's indemnity excludes IP infringement. Presence of a narrow Customer indemnity alone does not satisfy this rule.

Redline guidance:
If absent, insert a Vendor indemnity paragraph after the limitation-of-liability or warranty section (or the last numbered section before "General"). If one-sided, add the Vendor obligation and narrow Customer's.

Model language:
Vendor shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Customer and its affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (a) an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right; (b) Vendor's breach of applicable law; (c) any unauthorised access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor; or (d) Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct.


Claimed finding status: deviation

Finding rationale:
Section 8.1 gives an IBM indemnity only for third-party IP infringement claims relating to Materials or Base Components, and expressly makes that IBM's entire indemnity obligation; there is no indemnity for IBM's breach of applicable law, data breach caused by IBM, or IBM's gross negligence or wilful misconduct, as the playbook preferred position requires. Conversely, Customer's indemnity in 8.2 is broad, including any Services Recipient claim "related, directly or indirectly, to the Services", which goes well beyond Customer content and Customer breach of law. content.text:
**Finding: Compliant** — no edit proposed.

The agreement imposes no non-solicitation, no-hire, or anti-inducement restriction on Bluefly:

- **§ 14.8 (Personnel)** — the expected home for such a covenant — covers only supervision/direction of each party's own personnel, IBM's right to assign its people, and IBM's subcontracting rights. No hiring restriction.
- **§ 14.16 (Freedom of Action)** confirms each party is free to enter similar agreements with others, with no personnel carve-out.
- Targeted searches for "solicit", "hire", "recruit", "induce" and "employ" surface nothing beyond definitional and indemnity references to employees.

This lands on our preferred position (no non-solicit on Customer), so there is nothing to narrow — no duration, scope, or general-advertising carve-out analysis is needed. We should simply monitor any SOW or order-level terms for a re-introduced solicitation restriction; if one appears, the fallback (mutual, 12 months, personnel directly involved, advertising/unsolicited-approach carve-outs, no no-hire) would apply.

Rule:
ID: T4C
Title: Termination for convenience
Kind: parametric
Summary: We can leave on notice without penalty; the Vendor cannot walk away mid-term.
Severity: high
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.

Position — fallback:
Customer termination on 60–90 days' notice; early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees; Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term on 90 days' notice.

Position — walk-away:
No Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term; Vendor termination for convenience on fewer than 90 days' notice.

Rule:

Title: Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window
Kind: parametric
Summary: Renewals must be easy to exit and priced predictably.

Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Renewal only by mutual written agreement; or automatic 12-month renewals that Customer may opt out of on 30 days' notice, with a Vendor reminder 60 days before renewal; price increases capped at the lesser of CPI and 3 %.

Automatic renewal with a non-renewal notice window of no more than 60 days; price increases ≤ 5 %.

"automatically renew", "unless either party gives notice … days prior", renewal term length, price uplift language. Compute the notice window in days and the renewal term length.

Shorten the notice window (≤ 30, fallback ≤ 60 days), set renewal term to 12 months, cap uplift.

Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc.; counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation.

Rule:
ID: ASSIGN
Title: Assignment and change of control
Kind: parametric
Summary: We may assign to affiliates and successors; the Vendor may not exit on our change of control.
Severity: high
Category: assignment
Position — preferred:
Customer may assign without consent to an affiliate or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets; Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent (not to be unreasonably withheld) and never to a Customer competitor; no Vendor termination right on Customer's change of control.

Position — fallback:
Mutual right to assign to successors with written notice; consent for other assignments not unreasonably withheld.
Position — walk-away:
Blanket prohibition on Customer assignment with no M&A carve-out, or a Vendor right to terminate or re-price on Customer's change of control.

Detection guidance:
"may not assign", "change of control", "deemed an assignment", consent standards. Determine whether the restriction binds Customer symmetrically and whether change-of-control triggers any Vendor right.

Redline guidance:
Add the affiliate/successor carve-out for Customer; delete change-of-control termination rights against Customer.

reasons: Status is correctly classified as a deviation: Section 8.1 provides only an IP-infringement indemnity expressly stated to be IBM's 'entire obligation', with no prongs for breach of law, IBM-caused data breach, or gross negligence/wilful misconduct, while Section 8.2(a)(3) imposes a broad Customer indemnity for any Services Recipient claim 'related, directly or indirectly, to the Services'.

Redline is actionable and minimal: it adds the three missing IBM indemnity prongs (breach of law, unauthorised access/disclosure of Customer data, gross negligence/wilful misconduct) rather than rewriting Section 8.1, reuses the existing notice/control/cooperation conditions in 8.1(a)-(b), and sensibly confines the existing exclusions and the 'entire obligation' sentence to infringement claims so the new prongs are not swallowed by them.

Deletion of the broad Customer indemnity prong 8.2(a)(3) moves toward the preferred position (Customer indemnity limited to Customer content and Customer breach of law) and leaves the surrounding list grammatically intact since the deleted item was not the final enumerated item.

The failed deterministic check ('vendor indemnity for IP infringement present') is a false negative: IP infringement indemnity already exists in the original Section 8.1, so re-inserting it would not be the smallest edit; the redline correctly builds on it.

Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc.; counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation.

Rule:
ID: IP
Title: Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data
Kind: direction
Summary: We own what we pay for and everything we put in; no assignment of our IP or data to the Vendor.
Severity: critical
Category: ip-data
Position — preferred:
Customer owns deliverables and work product created for it (Vendor assigns); Vendor retains pre-existing IP and grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to any Vendor IP embedded in deliverables; Customer retains all rights in Customer Data; no joint ownership.

Position — fallback:
Vendor owns generic tools and know-how; Customer receives a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables for its business.

Position — walk-away:
Assignment of Customer IP or Customer Data to Vendor; joint ownership without an unrestricted right to exploit.
Detection guidance:
Ownership/assignment language: who owns "Deliverables", "Work Product", "Customer Data", improvements, feedback. Flag when Customer assigns IP or data to Vendor, when Vendor owns deliverables with no licence back, or when joint ownership is created. Vendor keeping ownership of its platform is fine.

Redline guidance:
Reverse the direction of the assignment or add the licence-back; add a Customer Data ownership sentence; delete joint ownership.

content.text:
**Finding: Compliant** — no edit proposed.

The agreement imposes no non-solicitation, no-hire, or anti-inducement restriction on Bluefly:

- **§ 14.8 (Personnel)** — the expected home for such a covenant — covers only supervision/direction of each party's own personnel, IBM's right to assign its people, and IBM's subcontracting rights. No hiring restriction.
- **§ 14.16 (Freedom of Action)** confirms each party is free to enter similar agreements with others, with no personnel carve-out.
- Targeted searches for "solicit", "hire", "recruit", "induce" and "employ" surface nothing beyond definitional and indemnity references to employees.

This lands on our preferred position (no non-solicit on Customer), so there is nothing to narrow — no duration, scope, or general-advertising carve-out analysis is needed. We should simply monitor any SOW or order-level terms for a re-introduced solicitation restriction; if one appears, the fallback (mutual, 12 months, personnel directly involved, advertising/unsolicited-approach carve-outs, no no-hire) would apply.

paragraphs.text: 3.3 Termination for Cause

Customer or IBM may terminate this Agreement for material breach of this Agreement by the other upon written notice containing the specific nature and dates of the material breach. The breaching party will have thirty (30) days from receipt of notice to cure such breach, except for nonpayment by Customer, which must be cured within seven (7) business days from receipt of notice. If such breach has not been timely cured, then the non-breaching party may immediately terminate this Agreement upon written notice; provided, however, it is understood that in the event IBM has so breached this Agreement IBM shall not be entitled to recover the early termination charges described in Section 3.4(b) below.
3.1 Term

This Agreement will be effective beginning on 12:01 a.m., Eastern Time, on the day after the date of last signature to these Base Terms ("Effective Date") and ending on the expiration and/or termination of all Service Option Attachments, unless the Agreement is terminated earlier in accordance with the terms herein. The term of each Service Option Attachment is as specified on the applicable Order Form.
3.5 Effect of&sbsp;Termination

Upon the date of termination, all Customer payment obligations accrued hereunder through the date of termination will become due and payable. The termination of selected Service Option Attachments will not affect Customer's obligation to pay charges under other Service Option Attachments.
4.1 Charges

Charges for applicable Services will be specified in Service Option Attachments and Order Forms. Charges can be specified as one-time, installment, recurring, or usage. IBM will invoice such Charges when they begin or are due as set forth in Service Option Attachments.

Rule:
ID: T4C
Title: Termination for convenience
Kind: parametric
Summary: We can leave on notice without penalty; the Vendor cannot walk away mid-term.
Severity: high
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.

Position — fallback:
Customer termination on 60–90 days' notice; early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees; Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term on 90 days' notice.

Position — walk-away:
No Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term; Vendor termination for convenience on fewer than 90 days' notice.

Detection guidance:
Find termination provisions. Determine which party may terminate without cause, the notice period, and any early-termination fee. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation (kind: missing behaviour); a Vendor convenience right on short notice is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Add or edit a Customer convenience right (30 days), delete/limit Vendor's convenience right, replace penalties with the fallback fee cap.

Model language:
Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.

Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc.; counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation.

Rule:
ID: RENEWAL
Title: Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window
Kind: parametric
Summary: Renewals must be easy to exit and priced predictably.
Severity: medium
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Renewal only by mutual written agreement; or automatic 12-month renewals that Customer may opt out of on 30 days' notice, with a Vendor reminder 60 days before renewal; price increases capped at the lesser of CPI and 3 %.

Position — fallback:
Automatic renewal with a non-renewal notice window of no more than 60 days; price increases ≤ 5 %.
Position — walk-away:
Non-renewal notice windows longer than 90 days, or automatic multi-year renewals.
Detection guidance:
"automatically renew", "unless either party gives notice … days prior", renewal term length, price uplift language. Compute the notice window in days and the renewal term length.

Redline guidance:
Shorten the notice window (≤ 30, fallback ≤ 60 days), set renewal term to 12 months, cap uplift.

Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc.; counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation.

Rule:
ID: ASSIGN
Title: Assignment and change of control
Kind: parametric
Summary: We may assign to affiliates and successors; the Vendor may not exit on our change of control.
Severity: high
Category: assignment
Position — preferred:
Customer may assign without consent to an affiliate or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets; Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent (not to be unreasonably withheld) and never to a Customer competitor; no Vendor termination right on Customer's change of control.

Position — fallback:
Mutual right to assign to successors with written notice; consent for other assignments not unreasonably withheld.
Position — walk-away:
Blanket prohibition on Customer assignment with no M&A carve-out, or a Vendor right to terminate or re-price on Customer's change of control.

Detection guidance:
"may not assign", "change of control", "deemed an assignment", consent standards. Determine whether the restriction binds Customer symmetrically and whether change-of-control triggers any Vendor right.

Redline guidance:
Add the affiliate/successor carve-out for Customer; delete change-of-control termination rights against Customer.

Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc.; counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation.

Rule:
ID: IP
Title: Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data
Kind: direction
Summary: We own what we pay for and everything we put in; no assignment of our IP or data to the Vendor.
Severity: critical
Category: ip-data
Position — preferred:
Customer owns deliverables and work product created for it (Vendor assigns); Vendor retains pre-existing IP and grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to any Vendor IP embedded in deliverables; Customer retains all rights in Customer Data; no joint ownership.

Position — fallback:
Vendor owns generic tools and know-how; Customer receives a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables for its business.

Position — walk-away:
Assignment of Customer IP or Customer Data to Vendor; joint ownership without an unrestricted right to exploit.
Detection guidance:
Ownership/assignment language: who owns "Deliverables", "Work Product", "Customer Data", improvements, feedback. Flag when Customer assigns IP or data to Vendor, when Vendor owns deliverables with no licence back, or when joint ownership is created. Vendor keeping ownership of its platform is fine.

Redline guidance:
Reverse the direction of the assignment or add the licence-back; add a Customer Data ownership sentence; delete joint ownership.

Rule:
ID: NOSOLICIT
Title: Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We accept only narrow, time-limited non-solicits with a general-advertising carve-out.
Severity: medium
Category: restrictive-covenants
Position — preferred:
No non-solicit on Customer.
Position — fallback:
Mutual non-solicit limited to personnel directly involved in the services, 12 months from the end of their involvement, with carve-outs for general advertisements and unsolicited approaches; no "no-hire".

Position — walk-away:
No-hire provisions, or restrictions longer than 24 months or covering all Vendor personnel.
Detection guidance:
"shall not solicit", "employ or engage", "no-hire", "induce … to leave". Determine duration, scope (all employees vs those involved) and whether a general-solicitation carve-out exists.

Redline guidance:
Narrow to the fallback with minimal edits (duration, scope, carve-out sentence). Delete any no-hire.

Claimed finding status: compliant

Finding rationale:
No non-solicitation, no-hire or anti-inducement covenant binds the Customer (Bluefly) anywhere in the agreement. Section 14.8 (Personnel), the expected home for such a restriction, addresses only each party's supervision of its own personnel, IBM's right to assign its personnel, and IBM's subcontracting rights. Full-text searches for "solicit", "hire", "recruit", "induce" and "employ" return no restrictive-covenant language (only definitional and indemnity references to employees), and Section 14.16 states merely that "Each party is free to enter into similar agreements with others" — a freedom-of-action provision, not a covenant. None of the detection triggers ("shall not solicit", "employ or engage", "no-hire", "induce ... to leave") appear. This is our preferred position (no non-solicit on Customer), so no redline or counterparty comment is warranted. The duration and general-solicitation carve-out sub-checks are inapplicable because there is no non-solicit clause to measure; we should monitor any SOW or order documents for a re-introduced restriction and, if one appears, hold to the fallback (mutual, 12 months from end of involvement, limited to personnel directly involved in the Services, carve-outs for general advertisements and unsolicited approaches, no no-hire).

Rule:
ID: T4C
Title: Termination for convenience
Kind: parametric
Summary: We can leave on notice without penalty; the Vendor cannot walk away mid-term.
Severity: high
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.

Position — fallback:
Customer termination on 60–90 days' notice; early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees; Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term on 90 days' notice.

Position — walk-away:
No Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term; Vendor termination for convenience on fewer than 90 days' notice.

Detection guidance:
Find termination provisions. Determine which party may terminate without cause, the notice period, and any early-termination fee. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation (kind: missing behaviour); a Vendor convenience right on short notice is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Add or edit a Customer convenience right (30 days), delete/limit Vendor's convenience right, replace penalties with the fallback fee cap.

Model language:
Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.

Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc.; counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation.

Rule:
ID: ASSIGN
Title: Assignment and change of control
Kind: parametric
Summary: We may assign to affiliates and successors; the Vendor may not exit on our change of control.
Severity: high
Category: assignment
Position — preferred:
Customer may assign without consent to an affiliate or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets; Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent (not to be unreasonably withheld) and never to a Customer competitor; no Vendor termination right on Customer's change of control.

Position — fallback:
Mutual right to assign to successors with written notice; consent for other assignments not unreasonably withheld.
Position — walk-away:
Blanket prohibition on Customer assignment with no M&A carve-out, or a Vendor right to terminate or re-price on Customer's change of control.

Detection guidance:
"may not assign", "change of control", "deemed an assignment", consent standards. Determine whether the restriction binds Customer symmetrically and whether change-of-control triggers any Vendor right.

Redline guidance:
Add the affiliate/successor carve-out for Customer; delete change-of-control termination rights against Customer.

Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc.; counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation.

Rule:
ID: IP
Title: Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data
Kind: direction
Summary: We own what we pay for and everything we put in; no assignment of our IP or data to the Vendor.
Severity: critical
Category: ip-data
Position — preferred:
Customer owns deliverables and work product created for it (Vendor assigns); Vendor retains pre-existing IP and grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to any Vendor IP embedded in deliverables; Customer retains all rights in Customer Data; no joint ownership.

Position — fallback:
Vendor owns generic tools and know-how; Customer receives a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables for its business.

Position — walk-away:
Assignment of Customer IP or Customer Data to Vendor; joint ownership without an unrestricted right to exploit.
Detection guidance:
Ownership/assignment language: who owns "Deliverables", "Work Product", "Customer Data", improvements, feedback. Flag when Customer assigns IP or data to Vendor, when Vendor owns deliverables with no licence back, or when joint ownership is created. Vendor keeping ownership of its platform is fine.

Redline guidance:
Reverse the direction of the assignment or add the licence-back; add a Customer Data ownership sentence; delete joint ownership.

**Finding: Compliant** — no edit proposed.

The agreement imposes no non-solicitation, no-hire, or anti-inducement restriction on Bluefly:

- **§ 14.8 (Personnel)** — the expected home for such a covenant — covers only supervision/direction of each party's own personnel, IBM's right to assign its people, and IBM's subcontracting rights. No hiring restriction.

This lands on our preferred position (no non-solicit on Customer), so there is nothing to narrow — no duration, scope, or general-advertising carve-out analysis is needed. We should simply monitor any SOW or order-level terms for a re-introduced solicitation restriction; if one appears, the fallback (mutual, 12 months, personnel directly involved, advertising/unsolicited-approach carve-outs, no no-hire) would apply.

Rule:
ID: T4C
Title: Termination for convenience
Kind: parametric
Summary: We can leave on notice without penalty; the Vendor cannot walk away mid-term.
Severity: high
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.

Position — fallback:
Customer termination on 60–90 days' notice; early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees; Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term on 90 days' notice.

Position — walk-away:
No Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term; Vendor termination for convenience on fewer than 90 days' notice.

Detection guidance:
Find termination provisions. Determine which party may terminate without cause, the notice period, and any early-termination fee. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation (kind: missing behaviour); a Vendor convenience right on short notice is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Add or edit a Customer convenience right (30 days), delete/limit Vendor's convenience right, replace penalties with the fallback fee cap.

Model language:
Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.

Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc.; counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation.

Rule:
ID: IP
Title: Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data
Kind: direction
Summary: We own what we pay for and everything we put in; no assignment of our IP or data to the Vendor.
Severity: critical
Category: ip-data
Position — preferred:
Customer owns deliverables and work product created for it (Vendor assigns); Vendor retains pre-existing IP and grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to any Vendor IP embedded in deliverables; Customer retains all rights in Customer Data; no joint ownership.

Position — fallback:
Vendor owns generic tools and know-how; Customer receives a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables for its business.

Position — walk-away:
Assignment of Customer IP or Customer Data to Vendor; joint ownership without an unrestricted right to exploit.
Detection guidance:
Ownership/assignment language: who owns "Deliverables", "Work Product", "Customer Data", improvements, feedback. Flag when Customer assigns IP or data to Vendor, when Vendor owns deliverables with no licence back, or when joint ownership is created. Vendor keeping ownership of its platform is fine.

Redline guidance:
Reverse the direction of the assignment or add the licence-back; add a Customer Data ownership sentence; delete joint ownership.

input.quote: 14.8 Personnel
input.rationale: Compliant with the preferred position: no non-solicitation, no-hire or anti-inducement covenant binds Bluefly (Customer) anywhere in the agreement. Section 14.8 (Personnel) — the expected home for such a restriction — contains only each party's responsibility for supervising its own personnel, IBM's right to determine assignment of its personnel, and IBM's right to subcontract to Subcontractors and Affiliates. Full-text searches for "solicit", "hire", "recruit" and "induce" return no hits, and "employ" appears only in definitional and indemnity contexts (employees of Customer/IBM), so none of the detection triggers ("shall not solicit", "employ or engage", "no-hire", "induce ... to leave") are present. Section 14.16 ("Each party is free to enter into similar agreements with others") is a freedom-of-action provision, not a restrictive covenant. Because there is no clause to narrow, no redline and no counterparty comment are proposed; the duration (12-month) and general-solicitation carve-out checks are inapplicable as they presuppose an existing non-solicit. If a restriction is introduced via SOW or order document, we would hold to the fallback: mutual, 12 months from the end of the individual's involvement, limited to personnel directly involved in the Services, with general-advertisement and unsolicited-approach carve-outs and no no-hire.

content.text:
**Finding: Compliant** — no edit proposed.

The agreement imposes no non-solicitation, no-hire, or anti-inducement restriction on Bluefly:

- **§ 14.8 (Personnel)** — the expected home for such a covenant — covers only supervision/direction of each party's own personnel, IBM's right to assign its people, and IBM's subcontracting rights. No hiring restriction.

Title: Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window
Kind: parametric
Summary: Renewals must be easy to exit and priced predictably.

Non-renewal notice windows longer than 90 days, or automatic multi-year renewals.

"automatically renew", "unless either party gives notice … days prior", renewal term length, price uplift language. Compute the notice window in days and the renewal term length.

Shorten the notice window (≤ 30, fallback ≤ 60 days), set renewal term to 12 months, cap uplift.

There is also no cap on renewal Charges: § 4.1 leaves Charges to the Service Option Attachments and Order Forms, so renewal pricing is unconstrained. Redline sets a 12-month renewal term, a 30-day Customer non-renewal notice (IBM retains 90 days), a 60-day IBM renewal reminder, and caps renewal uplift at the lesser of CPI and 3%.

proposal.summary: Set renewal term at 12 months, cut Customer's non-renewal notice to 30 days, add IBM renewal reminder and cap renewal price increases
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have set renewals at 12 months, reduced our non-renewal notice to 30 days (IBM retains 90 days), and added a 60-day renewal reminder plus a cap on renewal price increases at the lesser of CPI and 3%, so renewals stay easy to exit and predictably priced. If helpful, we can accept a 60-day notice window and a 5% uplift cap as a fallback.

ops.oldText: Each Service Option Attachment will renew automatically for an additional term equal in duration to the previous term of the applicable Service Option Attachment unless either party notifies the other party in writing at least ninety (90) days prior to the end of the then-current term for the applicable Service Option Attachment that it has elected to terminate such Service Option Attachment.
ops.newText: Each Service Option Attachment will renew automatically for an additional term of twelve (12) months unless (i) Customer notifies IBM in writing at least thirty (30) days, or (ii) IBM notifies Customer in writing at least ninety (90) days, prior to the end of the then-current term for the applicable Service Option Attachment that it has elected not to renew such Service Option Attachment. IBM will notify Customer in writing at least sixty (60) days prior to the end of the then-current term of the upcoming renewal and of any proposed change in Charges. Charges for any renewal term will not exceed the Charges in effect during the immediately preceding term by more than the lesser of (a) the percentage increase in the U.S. Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers over the preceding twelve (12) months and (b) three percent (3%).

Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc.; counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation.

Rule:
ID: T4C
Title: Termination for convenience
Kind: parametric
Summary: We can leave on notice without penalty; the Vendor cannot walk away mid-term.
Severity: high
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.

Position — fallback:
Customer termination on 60–90 days' notice; early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees; Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term on 90 days' notice.

Position — walk-away:
No Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term; Vendor termination for convenience on fewer than 90 days' notice.

Detection guidance:
Find termination provisions. Determine which party may terminate without cause, the notice period, and any early-termination fee. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation (kind: missing behaviour); a Vendor convenience right on short notice is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Add or edit a Customer convenience right (30 days), delete/limit Vendor's convenience right, replace penalties with the fallback fee cap.

Model language:
Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.

Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc.; counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation.

Rule:
ID: ASSIGN
Title: Assignment and change of control
Kind: parametric
Summary: We may assign to affiliates and successors; the Vendor may not exit on our change of control.
Severity: high
Category: assignment
Position — preferred:
Customer may assign without consent to an affiliate or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets; Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent (not to be unreasonably withheld) and never to a Customer competitor; no Vendor termination right on Customer's change of control.

Position — fallback:
Mutual right to assign to successors with written notice; consent for other assignments not unreasonably withheld.
Position — walk-away:
Blanket prohibition on Customer assignment with no M&A carve-out, or a Vendor right to terminate or re-price on Customer's change of control.

Detection guidance:
"may not assign", "change of control", "deemed an assignment", consent standards. Determine whether the restriction binds Customer symmetrically and whether change-of-control triggers any Vendor right.

Redline guidance:
Add the affiliate/successor carve-out for Customer; delete change-of-control termination rights against Customer.

Rule:
ID: NOSOLICIT
Title: Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We accept only narrow, time-limited non-solicits with a general-advertising carve-out.
Severity: medium
Category: restrictive-covenants
Position — preferred:
No non-solicit on Customer.
Position — fallback:
Mutual non-solicit limited to personnel directly involved in the services, 12 months from the end of their involvement, with carve-outs for general advertisements and unsolicited approaches; no "no-hire".

Position — walk-away:
No-hire provisions, or restrictions longer than 24 months or covering all Vendor personnel.
Detection guidance:
"shall not solicit", "employ or engage", "no-hire", "induce … to leave". Determine duration, scope (all employees vs those involved) and whether a general-solicitation carve-out exists.

Redline guidance:
Narrow to the fallback with minimal edits (duration, scope, carve-out sentence). Delete any no-hire.

Claimed finding status: compliant

Finding rationale:
Compliant with the preferred position: no non-solicitation, no-hire or anti-inducement covenant binds Bluefly (Customer) anywhere in the agreement. Section 14.8 (Personnel) — the expected home for such a restriction — contains only each party's responsibility for supervising its own personnel, IBM's right to determine assignment of its personnel, and IBM's right to subcontract to Subcontractors and Affiliates. Full-text searches for "solicit", "hire", "recruit" and "induce" return no hits, and "employ" appears only in definitional and indemnity contexts (employees of Customer/IBM), so none of the detection triggers ("shall not solicit", "employ or engage", "no-hire", "induce ... to leave") are present. Section 14.16 ("Each party is free to enter into similar agreements with others") is a freedom-of-action provision, not a restrictive covenant. Because there is no clause to narrow, no redline and no counterparty comment are proposed; the duration (12-month) and general-solicitation carve-out checks are inapplicable as they presuppose an existing non-solicit. If a restriction is introduced via SOW or order document, we would hold to the fallback: mutual, 12 months from the end of the individual's involvement, limited to personnel directly involved in the Services, with general-advertisement and unsolicited-approach carve-outs and no no-hire.

p0182: Each party is responsible for the supervision, direction, and control of its respective personnel. IBM reserves the right to determine the assignment of its personnel. IBM may subcontract portions of

Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc.; counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation.

Rule:
ID: T4C
Title: Termination for convenience
Kind: parametric
Summary: We can leave on notice without penalty; the Vendor cannot walk away mid-term.
Severity: high
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.

Position — fallback:
Customer termination on 60–90 days' notice; early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees; Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term on 90 days' notice.

Position — walk-away:
No Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term; Vendor termination for convenience on fewer than 90 days' notice.

Detection guidance:
Find termination provisions. Determine which party may terminate without cause, the notice period, and any early-termination fee. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation (kind: missing behaviour); a Vendor convenience right on short notice is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Add or edit a Customer convenience right (30 days), delete/limit Vendor's convenience right, replace penalties with the fallback fee cap.

Model language:
Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.

**Finding submitted: deviation (§ 3.2 Renewal, p0040).**

- **Renewal term:** auto-renews for a term "equal in duration to the previous term," so a multi-year initial term rolls into another multi-year term — a walk-away item under the rule.
- **Notice window:** 90 days, at the walk-away boundary and triple the preferred 30 days.
- **Pricing:** no renewal uplift cap; § 4.1 leaves Charges entirely to the Service Option Attachments/Order Forms.

Redline (validated, preferred level): fixed 12-month renewal term, 30-day Customer non-renewal notice (IBM keeps 90 days), a 60-day IBM renewal/price-change reminder, and renewal uplift capped at the lesser of CPI and 3%, with the 60-day / 5% fallback offered in the comment.

Rule:
ID: RENEWAL
Title: Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window
Kind: parametric
Summary: Renewals must be easy to exit and priced predictably.
Severity: medium
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Renewal only by mutual written agreement; or automatic 12-month renewals that Customer may opt out of on 30 days' notice, with a Vendor reminder 60 days before renewal; price increases capped at the lesser of CPI and 3 %.

Position — fallback:
Automatic renewal with a non-renewal notice window of no more than 60 days; price increases ≤ 5 %.
Position — walk-away:
Non-renewal notice windows longer than 90 days, or automatic multi-year renewals.
Detection guidance:
"automatically renew", "unless either party gives notice … days prior", renewal term length, price uplift language. Compute the notice window in days and the renewal term length.

Redline guidance:
Shorten the notice window (≤ 30, fallback ≤ 60 days), set renewal term to 12 months, cap uplift.

Claimed finding status: deviation

Finding rationale:
§ 3.2 auto-renews each Service Option Attachment for a term equal in duration to the prior term, so a multi-year initial term (set in the Order Form under § 3.1) renews automatically for another multi-year period — a walk-away item. The non-renewal notice window is 90 days, at the outer walk-away limit and well beyond the preferred 30 days (fallback 60). There is also no cap on renewal Charges: § 4.1 leaves Charges to the Service Option Attachments and Order Forms, so renewal pricing is unconstrained. Redline sets a 12-month renewal term, a 30-day Customer non-renewal notice (IBM retains 90 days), a 60-day IBM renewal reminder, and caps renewal uplift at the lesser of CPI and 3%.

Original paragraphs:
p0040: Each Service Option Attachment will renew automatically for an additional term equal in duration to the previous term of the applicable Service Option Attachment unless either party notifies the other party in writing at least ninety (90) days prior to the end of the then-current term for the applicable Service Option Attachment that it has elected to terminate such Service Option Attachment.

Resolved definitions:
none

Rendered redline:
p0040: Each Service Option Attachment will renew automatically for an additional term of twelve (12) months unless (i) Customer notifies IBM in writing at least thirty (30) days, or (ii) IBM notifies Customer in writing at least ninety (90) days, prior to the end of the then-current term for the applicable Service Option Attachment that it has elected not to renew such Service Option Attachment. IBM will notify Customer in writing at least sixty (60) days prior to the end of the then-current term of the upcoming renewal and of any proposed change in Charges. Charges for any renewal term will not exceed the Charges in effect during the immediately preceding term by more than the lesser of (a) the percentage increase in the U.S. Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers over the preceding twelve (12) months and (b) three percent (3%).

Comment:
[Playbook] We have set renewals at 12 months, reduced our non-renewal notice to 30 days (IBM retains 90 days), and added a 60-day renewal reminder plus a cap on renewal price increases at the lesser of CPI and 3%, so renewals stay easy to exit and predictably priced. If helpful, we can accept a 60-day notice window and a 5% uplift cap as a fallback.

Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc.; counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation.

Rule:
ID: ASSIGN
Title: Assignment and change of control
Kind: parametric
Summary: We may assign to affiliates and successors; the Vendor may not exit on our change of control.
Severity: high
Category: assignment
Position — preferred:
Customer may assign without consent to an affiliate or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets; Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent (not to be unreasonably withheld) and never to a Customer competitor; no Vendor termination right on Customer's change of control.

Position — fallback:
Mutual right to assign to successors with written notice; consent for other assignments not unreasonably withheld.
Position — walk-away:
Blanket prohibition on Customer assignment with no M&A carve-out, or a Vendor right to terminate or re-price on Customer's change of control.

Detection guidance:
"may not assign", "change of control", "deemed an assignment", consent standards. Determine whether the restriction binds Customer symmetrically and whether change-of-control triggers any Vendor right.

Redline guidance:
Add the affiliate/successor carve-out for Customer; delete change-of-control termination rights against Customer.

Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc.; counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation.

Rule:
ID: IP
Title: Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data
Kind: direction
Summary: We own what we pay for and everything we put in; no assignment of our IP or data to the Vendor.
Severity: critical
Category: ip-data
Position — preferred:
Customer owns deliverables and work product created for it (Vendor assigns); Vendor retains pre-existing IP and grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to any Vendor IP embedded in deliverables; Customer retains all rights in Customer Data; no joint ownership.

Position — fallback:
Vendor owns generic tools and know-how; Customer receives a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables for its business.

Position — walk-away:
Assignment of Customer IP or Customer Data to Vendor; joint ownership without an unrestricted right to exploit.
Detection guidance:
Ownership/assignment language: who owns "Deliverables", "Work Product", "Customer Data", improvements, feedback. Flag when Customer assigns IP or data to Vendor, when Vendor owns deliverables with no licence back, or when joint ownership is created. Vendor keeping ownership of its platform is fine.

Redline guidance:
Reverse the direction of the assignment or add the licence-back; add a Customer Data ownership sentence; delete joint ownership.

**Finding: deviation (medium)** — § 14.3 Choice of Law.

- **Governing law:** New York — matches our preferred position, no change needed.
- **Forum:** absent. There is no venue, jurisdiction, or arbitration provision anywhere in the Agreement (§ 14.4 is only a jury-trial waiver; § 14.14 only a two-year limitations period). No foreign arbitration seat, so no walk-away trigger.
- **Redline (validated, preferred level):** appended exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in New York County to the existing sentence, leaving the choice-of-law wording intact; Delaware/California/London courts flagged as acceptable fallback in the comment.

Rule:
ID: GOVLAW
Title: Governing law and venue
Kind: parametric
Summary: Accepted laws are New York, Delaware, California, or England and Wales; courts, not foreign arbitration.
Severity: medium
Category: governing-law
Position — preferred:
Laws of the State of New York; exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in New York County.
Position — fallback:
Delaware or California law and courts; or the laws of England and Wales with the courts of London.
Position — walk-away:
Vendor's home jurisdiction outside the accepted list with exclusive foreign venue, or mandatory arbitration seated abroad.
Detection guidance:
Find the governing-law clause; extract jurisdiction and dispute forum; note any arbitration seat.
Redline guidance:
Replace only the jurisdiction words and forum; keep the rest of the sentence intact.

Claimed finding status: deviation

Finding rationale:
Governing law is New York, which is our preferred position. However, the Agreement contains no venue or forum provision (no jurisdiction, venue, or arbitration clause anywhere in the document; § 14.4 waives jury trial and § 14.14 sets a limitations period only). The playbook requires courts in New York County with exclusive jurisdiction, so we add the forum language to the existing sentence without altering the choice of law. No arbitration seat exists, so there is no walk-away issue.

Original paragraphs:
p0171: This Agreement will be governed by the substantive laws of the State of New York, without regard for its conflict of laws provisions.

Resolved definitions:
none

Rendered redline:
p0171: This Agreement will be governed by the substantive laws of the State of New York, without regard for its conflict of laws provisions. The parties submit to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts located in New York County, New York for all disputes arising out of or related to this Agreement.

Comment:
[Playbook] New York law is acceptable to us, but the clause is silent on forum, so we have added exclusive jurisdiction in the state and federal courts in New York County to match the governing law and avoid disputes over venue. We can accept Delaware, California, or London courts as a fallback.

**Finding: deviation (§ 3.4 Termination for Convenience)**

- Customer's convenience right exists on one month's notice, and IBM has no convenience right anywhere in the Agreement (§ 3.3 is cause-only; § 11.3 is cause-based) — both consistent with our preferred position.

Rule:
ID: T4C
Title: Termination for convenience
Kind: parametric
Summary: We can leave on notice without penalty; the Vendor cannot walk away mid-term.
Severity: high
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.

Position — fallback:
Customer termination on 60–90 days' notice; early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees; Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term on 90 days' notice.

Position — walk-away:
No Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term; Vendor termination for convenience on fewer than 90 days' notice.

Detection guidance:
Find termination provisions. Determine which party may terminate without cause, the notice period, and any early-termination fee. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation (kind: missing behaviour); a Vendor convenience right on short notice is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Add or edit a Customer convenience right (30 days), delete/limit Vendor's convenience right, replace penalties with the fallback fee cap.

Model language:
Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.


Claimed finding status: deviation

Finding rationale:
Section 3.4 gives Customer a convenience right on one month's notice (consistent with our 30-day position) and IBM has no convenience right, but the right is conditioned on uncapped, externally-specified early termination charges and the Agreement provides no refund of prepaid charges (§ 3.5 only accelerates Customer's payment obligations). Our preferred position is convenience termination without penalty plus a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, so we deleted the open-ended charges and added the refund; the fallback of a cap at three months' charges is offered in the comment.

Original paragraphs:
p0044: Customer may terminate this Agreement (including all Service Option Attachments) or any Service Option Attachment (with the exception of any Service Option Attachment that is a prerequisite for the provision of Services under a non-terminated Service Option Attachment) for convenience at the end of any calendar month by:
p0045: a. providing at least one month's prior written notice to IBM; and
p0046: b. paying the applicable early termination charges, if any, specified in Attachment A and applicable Service Option Attachments.

Resolved definitions:
Customer: Under this e-business Hosting Agreement ("Agreement") between International Business Machines Corporation ("IBM") and Bluefly, Inc. ("Customer"), IBM will provide Web hosting and related services ("Services") to Customer. The Agreement includes these terms and conditions and the documents referenced herein ("Base Terms"), e-business hosting services order forms accepted by IBM ("Order Forms"), and the following attachments:
Service Option Attachments: c. all other applicable attachments referenced in the Order Forms for Services options selected by Customer ("Service Option Attachments").

Rendered redline:
p0046: b. paying all charges accrued for Services provided through the effective date of termination, in which case IBM will refund any prepaid charges for the period after the effective date of termination on a pro-rata basis and no early termination charges or other penalty will be payable by Customer.

Comment:
[Playbook] We have removed the open-ended early termination charges and added a pro-rata refund of prepaid charges, so our convenience right on one month's notice is exercisable without penalty. If IBM needs some recovery, we can accept a cap on early termination charges not exceeding three (3) months' charges for the terminated Service Option Attachment.

content.text:
**Finding: Deviation (high severity) — § 14.10 Assignment (p0188)**

The clause is one-sided. It restricts only our assignment (consent of IBM required), gives us a narrow successor carve-out limited to "merger, consolidation or acquisition" (no affiliate transfers, no sale of substantially all assets), and leaves IBM entirely free to assign — including to a competitor of ours. On the positive side, I confirmed there is no change-of-control termination or re-pricing right anywhere in the Agreement (no hits for "change of control"), so we are not at the walk-away threshold.

Redline submitted (validated ok): make the consent requirement mutual with the "not unreasonably withheld" standard applying both ways, bar IBM from assigning to a Customer competitor, expand our carve-out to Affiliates and to a sale of all or substantially all assets, and state expressly that our change of control gives IBM no termination, suspension or re-pricing right. Fallback offered in the comment if IBM resists full mutuality.

Rule:
ID: ASSIGN
Title: Assignment and change of control
Kind: parametric
Summary: We may assign to affiliates and successors; the Vendor may not exit on our change of control.
Severity: high
Category: assignment
Position — preferred:
Customer may assign without consent to an affiliate or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets; Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent (not to be unreasonably withheld) and never to a Customer competitor; no Vendor termination right on Customer's change of control.

Position — fallback:
Mutual right to assign to successors with written notice; consent for other assignments not unreasonably withheld.
Position — walk-away:
Blanket prohibition on Customer assignment with no M&A carve-out, or a Vendor right to terminate or re-price on Customer's change of control.

Detection guidance:
"may not assign", "change of control", "deemed an assignment", consent standards. Determine whether the restriction binds Customer symmetrically and whether change-of-control triggers any Vendor right.

Redline guidance:
Add the affiliate/successor carve-out for Customer; delete change-of-control termination rights against Customer.

Claimed finding status: deviation

Finding rationale:
Section 14.10 binds only Customer: we need IBM's consent to assign, there is no affiliate carve-out and no carve-out for a sale of substantially all assets, while IBM's own right to assign is unrestricted (including to our competitors). The playbook preferred position requires a Customer affiliate/successor carve-out, a mutual consent standard for other assignments, a bar on assignment to a Customer competitor, and confirmation that our change of control triggers no Vendor right. No change-of-control termination right appears elsewhere in the Agreement, so the redline simply makes the restriction mutual, adds the affiliate/asset-sale carve-out and states the change-of-control point for certainty.

Original paragraphs:
p0188: Customer will not assign this Agreement or any of its rights hereunder without the prior written consent of IBM, such consent not to be unreasonably withheld. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Customer may assign this Agreement to a successor organization by merger, consolidation or acquisition. Any attempted assignment in violation of the foregoing will be void. In any permitted assignment, Customer will remain liable for its obligations hereunder.

Resolved definitions:
Customer: Under this e-business Hosting Agreement ("Agreement") between International Business Machines Corporation ("IBM") and Bluefly, Inc. ("Customer"), IBM will provide Web hosting and related services ("Services") to Customer. The Agreement includes these terms and conditions and the documents referenced herein ("Base Terms"), e-business hosting services order forms accepted by IBM ("Order Forms"), and the following attachments:

Rendered redline:
p0188: Neither party will assign this Agreement or any of its rights hereunder without the prior written consent of the other party, such consent not to be unreasonably withheld, and IBM will not assign this Agreement to a competitor of Customer. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Customer may assign this Agreement, without IBM's consent, to an Affiliate or to a successor organization by merger, consolidation, acquisition or sale of all or substantially all of its assets, and no change of control of Customer will give IBM any right to terminate, suspend or re-price this Agreement. Any attempted assignment in violation of the foregoing will be void. In any permitted assignment, Customer will remain liable for its obligations hereunder.

Comment:
[Playbook] We have made the assignment restriction mutual and added our standard carve-out allowing us to assign to an Affiliate or to a successor by merger or sale of substantially all assets without consent, plus confirmation that a change of control does not give IBM a termination or re-pricing right. Our fallback is a mutual right to assign to successors on written notice with consent for other assignments not unreasonably withheld.

Vendor owns generic tools and know-how; Customer receives a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables for its business.

Assignment of Customer IP or Customer Data to Vendor; joint ownership without an unrestricted right to exploit.

Ownership/assignment language: who owns "Deliverables", "Work Product", "Customer Data", improvements, feedback. Flag when Customer assigns IP or data to Vendor, when Vendor owns deliverables with no licence back, or when joint ownership is created. Vendor keeping ownership of its platform is fine.

Reverse the direction of the assignment or add the licence-back; add a Customer Data ownership sentence; delete joint ownership.

Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc.; counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation.

Rule:
ID: LICENSE
Title: Licence grant scope
Kind: parametric
Summary: The licence must cover our affiliates and contractors and must not be revocable at will.
Severity: high
Category: licence
Position — preferred:
Licence extends to Customer's affiliates and to contractors acting on Customer's behalf; paid-up licences are perpetual and irrevocable; subscription licences terminable only for uncured material breach; transferable to successors.

Position — fallback:
Affiliates covered on written notice; transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction.
Position — walk-away:
Licence revocable at Vendor's discretion; affiliates and contractors excluded with no path to add them.
Detection guidance:
Find the grant clause: "non-exclusive, non-transferable", "revocable", "solely for Customer's internal use", whether affiliates/contractors are named, term of the licence.

Redline guidance:
Insert "and its Affiliates and contractors acting on its behalf", delete "revocable", add successor transfer.

paragraphs.text: 11.3 Suspected Violations

IBM reserves the right to investigate potential violations of the representations and warranties in Subsection 11.2(b). If IBM reasonably determines that a breach of any such warranty has occurred, then IBM may, in its sole and reasonable discretion:
a. restrict Customer's access to the Services;
b. remove or require removal of any offending Content;
c. terminate this Agreement for cause; and/or
d. exercise other rights and remedies, at law or in equity.

Except in an emergency or as may otherwise be required by law, before undertaking the activities in Subsection 11.3(a) or 11.3(b), IBM will attempt to notify Customer by any reasonably practical means under the circumstances, such as, without limitation, by telephone or e-mail.

Customer will promptly notify IBM of any event or circumstance related to this Agreement, Customer's use of the Services, or Content of which Customer becomes aware that could lead to a claim or demand against IBM, and Customer will provide all relevant information relating to such event or circumstance to IBM at IBM's request.
13.2 Acceptable Use Policy
IBM, in its reasonable discretion, may modify the Acceptable Use Policy upon thirty (30) days' notice to Customer.

Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc.; counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation.

Rule:
ID: AUDIT
Title: Audit rights against Customer
Kind: parametric
Summary: Audits of our usage must be rare, notified, off-site where possible and at the Vendor's cost.
Severity: medium
Category: audit
Position — preferred:
No more than once per 12 months, on 30 days' written notice, during business hours, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, at Vendor's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5 %; no direct access to Customer systems.

Position — fallback:
Once per year on 15 days' notice; Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 10 %.
Position — walk-away:
Unlimited or unannounced audits, or remote access to Customer systems.
Detection guidance:
Find audit/inspection/verification rights binding Customer; extract frequency, notice, cost allocation, system access.
Redline guidance:
Insert the frequency/notice/cost limits with minimal edits; delete system-access language.

Kind: direction

Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc.; counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation.

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:

Rule:

Title: Vendor insurance
Kind: missing
Summary: Vendors that touch our data or premises carry standard insurance.

E&O USD 1M and cyber USD 2M.

Vendor shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term and for one (1) year thereafter: commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; and, where Vendor processes Customer Data, cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000. Vendor shall provide certificates of insurance on request.

input.summary: Make Customer-ownership (Type I) the default for Materials created for us, limit IBM-owned Type II Materials to pre-existing/generic IP with a broader licence back, restrict IBM's licence in Customer-owned Materials to performing the Services, and confirm we retain all rights in Content and Customer Components with no joint ownership.
input.comment: [Playbook] We own what we pay for: Materials created for us during the Services should default to Type I (Customer-owned), with IBM retaining only its pre-existing and generic IP under a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence back that is not limited to internal Enterprise use, and IBM's licence in our Materials limited to performing the Services. We have also confirmed that we retain all rights in our Content and Customer Components and that nothing is jointly owned or assigned to IBM. If IBM cannot move the default, we can accept IBM ownership of generic tools and know-how provided we receive the broad licence in paragraph (c) and the ownership confirmation in paragraph (e).

Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc.; counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation.

Rule:
ID: IP
Title: Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data
Kind: direction
Summary: We own what we pay for and everything we put in; no assignment of our IP or data to the Vendor.
Severity: critical
Category: ip-data
Position — preferred:
Customer owns deliverables and work product created for it (Vendor assigns); Vendor retains pre-existing IP and grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to any Vendor IP embedded in deliverables; Customer retains all rights in Customer Data; no joint ownership.

Position — fallback:
Vendor owns generic tools and know-how; Customer receives a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables for its business.

Position — walk-away:
Assignment of Customer IP or Customer Data to Vendor; joint ownership without an unrestricted right to exploit.
Detection guidance:
Ownership/assignment language: who owns "Deliverables", "Work Product", "Customer Data", improvements, feedback. Flag when Customer assigns IP or data to Vendor, when Vendor owns deliverables with no licence back, or when joint ownership is created. Vendor keeping ownership of its platform is fine.

Redline guidance:
Reverse the direction of the assignment or add the licence-back; add a Customer Data ownership sentence; delete joint ownership.

input.summary: Make Customer-ownership (Type I) the default for Materials created for us, limit IBM-owned Type II Materials to pre-existing/generic IP with a broader licence back, restrict IBM's licence in Customer-owned Materials to performing the Services, and confirm we retain all rights in Content and Customer Components with no joint ownership.
input.comment: [Playbook] We own what we pay for: Materials created for us during the Services should default to Type I (Customer-owned), with IBM retaining only its pre-existing and generic IP under a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence back that is not limited to internal Enterprise use, and IBM's licence in our Materials limited to performing the Services. We have also confirmed that we retain all rights in our Content and Customer Components and that nothing is jointly owned or assigned to IBM. If IBM cannot move the default, we can accept IBM ownership of generic tools and know-how provided we receive the broad licence in paragraph (c) and the ownership confirmation in paragraph (e).

Title: Audit rights against Customer
Kind: parametric
Summary: Audits of our usage must be rare, notified, off-site where possible and at the Vendor's cost.

Category: audit

No more than once per 12 months, on 30 days' written notice, during business hours, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, at Vendor's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5 %; no direct access to Customer systems.

Unlimited or unannounced audits, or remote access to Customer systems.

Find audit/inspection/verification rights binding Customer; extract frequency, notice, cost allocation, system access.

Insert the frequency/notice/cost limits with minimal edits; delete system-access language.

Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc.; counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation.

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

input.quote: a. IBM will specify Materials to be delivered to Customer. IBM will identify them as being "Type I Materials," "Type II Materials," or otherwise as Customer and IBM agree in writing. If not specified, Materials will be considered Type II Materials.
input.rationale: Section 7 reverses our required ownership direction. Type II Materials expressly include works "created during the Service performance period," IBM owns them, and Type II is the default where nothing is specified — so deliverables we pay for default to IBM ownership with only an irrevocable licence limited to use "within Customer's Enterprise only" (no modification or sublicensing rights). Conversely, where we do own Type I Materials, we must grant IBM an irrevocable worldwide licence to distribute them externally and to authorise others to do the same, which lets IBM exploit our work product beyond performing the Services. The Agreement also nowhere confirms that we retain ownership of our Content, Customer Components and data (11.6 only allocates responsibility; 14.17 grants no rights beyond those expressly stated). The redline makes Type I the default, confines IBM ownership to pre-existing/generic IP with a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence back covering IBM IP embedded in deliverables, narrows IBM's licence in our Materials to performing the Services, and adds a Customer Data/no-joint-ownership provision.

proposal.summary: Make Customer-ownership (Type I) the default for Materials created for us, limit IBM-owned Type II Materials to pre-existing/generic IP with a broader licence back, restrict IBM's licence in Customer-owned Materials to performing the Services, and confirm we retain all rights in Content and Customer Components with no joint ownership.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We own what we pay for: Materials created for us during the Services should default to Type I (Customer-owned), with IBM retaining only its pre-existing and generic IP under a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence back that is not limited to internal Enterprise use, and IBM's licence in our Materials limited to performing the Services. We have also confirmed that we retain all rights in our Content and Customer Components and that nothing is jointly owned or assigned to IBM. If IBM cannot move the default, we can accept IBM ownership of generic tools and know-how provided we receive the broad licence in paragraph (c) and the ownership confirmation in paragraph (e).

ops.oldText: If not specified, Materials will be considered Type II Materials.
ops.newText: If not specified, Materials will be considered Type I Materials.

ops.oldText: distribute (internally and externally) copies of, and prepare derivative works based on Type I Materials; and 2. the right to authorize others to do any of the same.
ops.newText: distribute internally copies of, and prepare derivative works based on Type I Materials, in each case solely as necessary to perform the Services for Customer; and 2. the right to authorize its Subcontractors to do any of the same solely for that purpose.

ops.oldText: c. Type II Materials are those, created during the Service performance period or otherwise (such as those that preexist the Service), in which IBM or third parties have all right, title, and interest (including ownership of copyright). IBM will deliver one copy of the specified Materials to Customer. IBM grants Customer an irrevocable, nonexclusive, worldwide, paid-up license to use, execute, reproduce, display, perform, and distribute, within Customer's Enterprise only, copies of Type II Materials.
ops.newText: c. Type II Materials are those that preexist the Service performance period, or that consist of IBM's generic tools, know-how or platform components, in which IBM or third parties have all right, title, and interest (including ownership of copyright). IBM will deliver one copy of the specified Materials to Customer. IBM grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, nonexclusive, worldwide, royalty-free, paid-up license to use, execute, reproduce, display, perform, modify, prepare derivative works based on, and distribute copies of Type II Materials, and to sublicense the foregoing rights to its Enterprise and to contractors acting on its behalf, in each case for Customer's business purposes, including any Type II Materials incorporated in or necessary to use Type I Materials.

ops.text: e. Customer retains all right, title, and interest (including all intellectual property rights) in and to the Content, the Customer Components, and all other data Customer or its Services Recipients provide or generate through the Services. Nothing in this Agreement assigns or transfers to IBM any ownership of the Content, the Customer Components, such data, or any Type I Materials, and no Materials, work product, or data will be jointly owned by the parties.

Reverse the direction of the assignment or add the licence-back; add a Customer Data ownership sentence; delete joint ownership.
