input.quote: a. IBM will specify Materials to be delivered to Customer. IBM will identify them as being "Type I Materials," "Type II Materials," or otherwise as Customer and IBM agree in writing. If not specified, Materials will be considered Type II Materials.
input.rationale: Section 7 reverses our required ownership direction. Type II Materials expressly include works "created during the Service performance period," IBM owns them, and Type II is the default where nothing is specified — so deliverables we pay for default to IBM ownership with only an irrevocable licence limited to use "within Customer's Enterprise only" (no modification or sublicensing rights). Conversely, where we do own Type I Materials, we must grant IBM an irrevocable worldwide licence to distribute them externally and to authorise others to do the same, which lets IBM exploit our work product beyond performing the Services. The Agreement also nowhere confirms that we retain ownership of our Content, Customer Components and data (11.6 only allocates responsibility; 14.17 grants no rights beyond those expressly stated). The redline makes Type I the default, confines IBM ownership to pre-existing/generic IP with a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence back covering IBM IP embedded in deliverables, narrows IBM's licence in our Materials to performing the Services, and adds a Customer Data/no-joint-ownership provision.

Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc.; counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation.

Rule:
ID: LICENSE
Title: Licence grant scope
Kind: parametric
Summary: The licence must cover our affiliates and contractors and must not be revocable at will.
Severity: high
Category: licence
Position — preferred:
Licence extends to Customer's affiliates and to contractors acting on Customer's behalf; paid-up licences are perpetual and irrevocable; subscription licences terminable only for uncured material breach; transferable to successors.

Position — fallback:
Affiliates covered on written notice; transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction.
Position — walk-away:
Licence revocable at Vendor's discretion; affiliates and contractors excluded with no path to add them.
Detection guidance:
Find the grant clause: "non-exclusive, non-transferable", "revocable", "solely for Customer's internal use", whether affiliates/contractors are named, term of the licence.

Redline guidance:
Insert "and its Affiliates and contractors acting on its behalf", delete "revocable", add successor transfer.

Rule:
ID: AUDIT
Title: Audit rights against Customer
Kind: parametric
Summary: Audits of our usage must be rare, notified, off-site where possible and at the Vendor's cost.
Severity: medium
Category: audit
Position — preferred:
No more than once per 12 months, on 30 days' written notice, during business hours, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, at Vendor's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5 %; no direct access to Customer systems.

Position — fallback:
Once per year on 15 days' notice; Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 10 %.
Position — walk-away:
Unlimited or unannounced audits, or remote access to Customer systems.
Detection guidance:
Find audit/inspection/verification rights binding Customer; extract frequency, notice, cost allocation, system access.
Redline guidance:
Insert the frequency/notice/cost limits with minimal edits; delete system-access language.

paragraphs.text: 4.1 Charges

Charges for applicable Services will be specified in Service Option Attachments and Order Forms. Charges can be specified as one-time, installment, recurring, or usage. IBM will invoice such Charges when they begin or are due as set forth in Service Option Attachments.
4.2 Payment

IBM invoices will specify the amount due. Payment is due upon receipt and payable as specified in such invoice. Customer agrees to pay accordingly, including any late payment fees. Payment will be made in United States dollars.
3.4 Termination for Convenience

Customer may terminate this Agreement (including all Service Option Attachments) or any Service Option Attachment (with the exception of any Service Option Attachment that is a prerequisite for the provision of Services under a non-terminated Service Option Attachment) for convenience at the end of any calendar month by:
a. providing at least one month's prior written notice to IBM; and
b. paying the applicable early termination charges, if any, specified in Attachment A and applicable Service Option Attachments.
In the event that Customer exercises its rights under this Section 3.4, IBM shall continue to fulfill all of its duties and obligations following the notice date and until the final termination date.
11.1 Services Support

Customer will comply with its responsibilities to support the Services as specified in Attachment A and in applicable Service Option Attachments. Such obligations are to be performed at no charge to IBM. IBM's obligations are contingent on Customer meeting such support obligations.

Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc.; counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation.

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

content.text:
**Finding submitted: deviation (IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data), confidence 0.85.**

What I found in Section 7 (Materials), which sits inside the mis-numbered §5.4 block:

- **Default ownership runs to IBM.** §7(a) makes Type II the default, and §7(c) defines Type II to include Materials "created during the Service performance period" — so deliverables we pay for default to IBM ownership.
- **Licence back is too narrow.** Our Type II licence is use/reproduce/display/distribute "within Customer's Enterprise only" — no modification, no derivative works, no contractor or sublicence rights, and "Enterprise" is capped at US entities.
- **Our own work product is licensed out broadly.** §7(b) requires us to grant IBM an irrevocable, worldwide licence to distribute Type I Materials externally and to authorise others to do the same — exploitation beyond performing the Services.
- **No Customer Data ownership statement.** §11.6 only allocates responsibility for Content, and §14.17 grants nothing beyond express licences, so there is no affirmation that we retain rights in Content/Customer Components.

Redline (validated ok:true): flip the default to Type I; confine Type II to IBM's pre-existing/generic tools and know-how with a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free, sublicensable licence covering IBM IP embedded in deliverables; limit IBM's licence in our Type I Materials to performing the Services; and add a new §7(e) confirming we retain all rights in Content, Customer Components and data, with no assignment to IBM and no joint ownership. The comment flags the fallback (IBM keeps generic tools/know-how) if IBM will not move the default.

Deterministic checks are heuristics (regular expressions and a changed-character ratio), not verdicts: a failed regex may simply be a phrasing variant, and a high changed-character ratio is acceptable when the rule genuinely requires rewriting the clause (for example replacing a governing-law sentence or deleting a take-or-pay obligation). Weigh them as evidence and decide on substance: does the redline reach the playbook position with the smallest edit that does so, and is the comment accurate?

Rule:
ID: IP
Title: Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data
Kind: direction
Summary: We own what we pay for and everything we put in; no assignment of our IP or data to the Vendor.
Severity: critical
Category: ip-data
Position — preferred:
Customer owns deliverables and work product created for it (Vendor assigns); Vendor retains pre-existing IP and grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to any Vendor IP embedded in deliverables; Customer retains all rights in Customer Data; no joint ownership.

Position — fallback:
Vendor owns generic tools and know-how; Customer receives a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables for its business.

Position — walk-away:
Assignment of Customer IP or Customer Data to Vendor; joint ownership without an unrestricted right to exploit.
Detection guidance:
Ownership/assignment language: who owns "Deliverables", "Work Product", "Customer Data", improvements, feedback. Flag when Customer assigns IP or data to Vendor, when Vendor owns deliverables with no licence back, or when joint ownership is created. Vendor keeping ownership of its platform is fine.

Redline guidance:
Reverse the direction of the assignment or add the licence-back; add a Customer Data ownership sentence; delete joint ownership.

Claimed finding status: deviation

Finding rationale:
Section 7 reverses our required ownership direction. Type II Materials expressly include works "created during the Service performance period," IBM owns them, and Type II is the default where nothing is specified — so deliverables we pay for default to IBM ownership with only an irrevocable licence limited to use "within Customer's Enterprise only" (no modification or sublicensing rights). Conversely, where we do own Type I Materials, we must grant IBM an irrevocable worldwide licence to distribute them externally and to authorise others to do the same, which lets IBM exploit our work product beyond performing the Services. The Agreement also nowhere confirms that we retain ownership of our Content, Customer Components and data (11.6 only allocates responsibility; 14.17 grants no rights beyond those expressly stated). The redline makes Type I the default, confines IBM ownership to pre-existing/generic IP with a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence back covering IBM IP embedded in deliverables, narrows IBM's licence in our Materials to performing the Services, and adds a Customer Data/no-joint-ownership provision.

Original paragraphs:
p0082: a. IBM will specify Materials to be delivered to Customer. IBM will identify them as being "Type I Materials," "Type II Materials," or otherwise as Customer and IBM agree in writing. If not specified, Materials will be considered Type II Materials.
p0084: 1. an irrevocable, nonexclusive, worldwide, paid-up license to use, execute, reproduce, display, perform, distribute (internally and externally) copies of, and prepare derivative works based on Type I Materials; and 2. the right to authorize others to do any of the same.
p0085: c. Type II Materials are those, created during the Service performance period or otherwise (such as those that preexist the Service), in which IBM or third parties have all right, title, and interest (including ownership of copyright). IBM will deliver one copy of the specified Materials to Customer. IBM grants Customer an irrevocable, nonexclusive, worldwide, paid-up license to use, execute, reproduce, display, perform, and distribute, within Customer's Enterprise only, copies of Type II Materials.
p0086: d. The parties agree to reproduce the copyright notice and any other legend of ownership on any copies made under the licenses granted in this Section 7.

Resolved definitions:

("Customer"), IBM will provide Web hosting and related services ("Services") to Customer. The Agreement includes these terms and conditions and the documents referenced herein ("Base Terms"), e-business hosting services order forms accepted by IBM ("Order Forms"), and the following attachments:

Rendered redline:
p0082: a. IBM will specify Materials to be delivered to Customer. IBM will identify them as being "Type I Materials," "Type II Materials," or otherwise as Customer and IBM agree in writing. If not specified, Materials will be considered Type I Materials.
p0084: 1. an irrevocable, nonexclusive, worldwide, paid-up license to use, execute, reproduce, display, perform, distribute internally copies of, and prepare derivative works based on Type I Materials, in each case solely as necessary to perform the Services for Customer; and 2. the right to authorize its Subcontractors to do any of the same solely for that purpose.
p0085: c. Type II Materials are those that preexist the Service performance period, or that consist of IBM's generic tools, know-how or platform components, in which IBM or third parties have all right, title, and interest (including ownership of copyright). IBM will deliver one copy of the specified Materials to Customer. IBM grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, nonexclusive, worldwide, royalty-free, paid-up license to use, execute, reproduce, display, perform, modify, prepare derivative works based on, and distribute copies of Type II Materials, and to sublicense the foregoing rights to its Enterprise and to contractors acting on its behalf, in each case for Customer's business purposes, including any Type II Materials incorporated in or necessary to use Type I Materials.

e. Customer retains all right, title, and interest (including all intellectual property rights) in and to the Content, the Customer Components, and all other data Customer or its Services Recipients provide or generate through the Services. Nothing in this Agreement assigns or transfers to IBM any ownership of the Content, the Customer Components, such data, or any Type I Materials, and no Materials, work product, or data will be jointly owned by the parties.

Comment:
[Playbook] We own what we pay for: Materials created for us during the Services should default to Type I (Customer-owned), with IBM retaining only its pre-existing and generic IP under a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence back that is not limited to internal Enterprise use, and IBM's licence in our Materials limited to performing the Services. We have also confirmed that we retain all rights in our Content and Customer Components and that nothing is jointly owned or assigned to IBM. If IBM cannot move the default, we can accept IBM ownership of generic tools and know-how provided we receive the broad licence in paragraph (c) and the ownership confirmation in paragraph (e).

Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc.; counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation.

Rule:
ID: AUDIT
Title: Audit rights against Customer
Kind: parametric
Summary: Audits of our usage must be rare, notified, off-site where possible and at the Vendor's cost.
Severity: medium
Category: audit
Position — preferred:
No more than once per 12 months, on 30 days' written notice, during business hours, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, at Vendor's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5 %; no direct access to Customer systems.

Position — fallback:
Once per year on 15 days' notice; Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 10 %.
Position — walk-away:
Unlimited or unannounced audits, or remote access to Customer systems.
Detection guidance:
Find audit/inspection/verification rights binding Customer; extract frequency, notice, cost allocation, system access.
Redline guidance:
Insert the frequency/notice/cost limits with minimal edits; delete system-access language.

paragraphs.text: 3.5 Effect of&sbsp;Termination

Upon the date of termination, all Customer payment obligations accrued hereunder through the date of termination will become due and payable. The termination of selected Service Option Attachments will not affect Customer's obligation to pay charges under other Service Option Attachments.
9.2 Customer's Limitation of Liability

Circumstances may arise where, because of a default on Customer's part or other liability, IBM is entitled to recover damages from Customer. Regardless of the basis on which IBM is entitled to claim damages from Customer (including fundamental breach, negligence, misrepresentation, or other contract or tort claim), Customer is liable for no more than:
a. Indemnification payments as provided in Section 8.2;
b. damages for bodily injury (including death) and damage to real property and tangible personal property; and

(c) the amount of any other actual direct damages, up to the greater of $100,000 or the charges paid by Customer to IBM for the Services in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the accrual of the first claim related to the Services. The foregoing limit also applies to any of Customer's Affiliates. It is the cumulative maximum for which Customer and its Affiliates are collectively responsible. Under no circumstances is Customer or its Affiliates liable for any third party claims against IBM for damages (other than those
expressly provided in Subsections 9.2(a) and 9.2(b)).

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

Rule:
ID: INSURANCE
Title: Vendor insurance
Kind: missing
Summary: Vendors that touch our data or premises carry standard insurance.
Severity: low
Category: insurance
Position — preferred:
Commercial general liability USD 1M per occurrence / 2M aggregate; professional (E&O) USD 2M; cyber/privacy USD 5M for vendors processing Customer Data; workers' compensation as required by law; certificates on request.

Position — fallback:
E&O USD 1M and cyber USD 2M.
Position — walk-away:
No insurance for a vendor that processes personal data or works on our premises.
Detection guidance:
Look for an insurance clause; if absent for a services/hosting vendor, deviation (insert).

Insert a short insurance paragraph in the general/miscellaneous section.

Vendor shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term and for one (1) year thereafter: commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; and, where Vendor processes Customer Data, cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000. Vendor shall provide certificates of insurance on request.

Rule:
ID: MINCOMMIT
Title: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not take-or-pay without an exit.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No minimum commitment; fees are for usage or ordered services only.
Position — fallback:
Commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.
Position — walk-away:
Multi-year take-or-pay commitments with no reduction or termination right.
Detection guidance:
"minimum", "commit to purchase", "take or pay", "shortfall", volume caps on Customer usage. Commitments the Vendor makes to us are fine.
Redline guidance:
Delete or narrow to the fallback with minimal edits; replace shortfall penalties with a true-up.

Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc.; counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation.

Rule:
ID: LICENSE
Title: Licence grant scope
Kind: parametric
Summary: The licence must cover our affiliates and contractors and must not be revocable at will.
Severity: high
Category: licence
Position — preferred:
Licence extends to Customer's affiliates and to contractors acting on Customer's behalf; paid-up licences are perpetual and irrevocable; subscription licences terminable only for uncured material breach; transferable to successors.

Position — fallback:
Affiliates covered on written notice; transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction.
Position — walk-away:
Licence revocable at Vendor's discretion; affiliates and contractors excluded with no path to add them.
Detection guidance:
Find the grant clause: "non-exclusive, non-transferable", "revocable", "solely for Customer's internal use", whether affiliates/contractors are named, term of the licence.

Redline guidance:
Insert "and its Affiliates and contractors acting on its behalf", delete "revocable", add successor transfer.

paragraphs.text: 11.2 Representations and Warranties
Customer represents and warrants that:

a. it has the requisite corporate power and authority to execute, deliver and perform its obligations under this Agreement; Customer has no contractual or other obligation that (i) restricts or prohibits Customer's execution or performance of this Agreement, or (ii) Customer will breach in connection with the execution or performance of this Agreement; and
b. its use of the Services and all Content will comply with the Acceptable Use Policy.
5.3 Security
a. Customer acknowledges that IBM does not control the transfer of data over telecommunications facilities, including the Internet.

b. Subject to the other disclaimers contained herein, IBM will implement the security features specified herein, including the IBM perform security obligations identified in Section 8.0 of the Facilities Services Service Option Attachment. However, IBM does not warrant secure operation of the Services or that it will be able to prevent third party disruptions of the e-business Hosting Environment or Customer Components.

c. Customer acknowledges that IBM offers numerous security options, specified in Service Option Attachments. Customer is responsible for selecting on Order Forms the set of security options that it determines meet Customer's needs.
d. Customer agrees that IBM shall have no liability for any provision of security-related services or advice that IBM may voluntarily provide outside the scope of selected Service Option Attachments.

Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc.; counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation.

Rule:
ID: AUDIT
Title: Audit rights against Customer
Kind: parametric
Summary: Audits of our usage must be rare, notified, off-site where possible and at the Vendor's cost.
Severity: medium
Category: audit
Position — preferred:
No more than once per 12 months, on 30 days' written notice, during business hours, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, at Vendor's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5 %; no direct access to Customer systems.

Position — fallback:
Once per year on 15 days' notice; Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 10 %.
Position — walk-away:
Unlimited or unannounced audits, or remote access to Customer systems.
Detection guidance:
Find audit/inspection/verification rights binding Customer; extract frequency, notice, cost allocation, system access.
Redline guidance:
Insert the frequency/notice/cost limits with minimal edits; delete system-access language.

Rule:
ID: LD
Title: Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer
Kind: direction
Summary: Service credits to us are welcome; liquidated damages against us are not.
Severity: high
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer.
Position — fallback:
Early-termination fee capped at 3 months' fees as the sole liquidated amount.
Position — walk-away:
Liquidated damages exceeding the remaining contract value or triggered by minor breaches.
Detection guidance:
Identify liquidated damages, penalties, minimum fees on termination, "shall pay … as liquidated damages". Flag only when Customer pays. Service credits or LDs payable by Vendor to Customer are compliant.

Redline guidance:
Delete the Customer-payable LD; if an early-termination fee is unavoidable, cap it at 3 months' fees.

Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc.; counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation.

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

ID: INSURANCE
Title: Vendor insurance
Kind: missing
Summary: Vendors that touch our data or premises carry standard insurance.

E&O USD 1M and cyber USD 2M.

No insurance for a vendor that processes personal data or works on our premises.

Vendor shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term and for one (1) year thereafter: commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; and, where Vendor processes Customer Data, cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000. Vendor shall provide certificates of insurance on request.

paragraphs.text: 3.3 Termination for Cause

Customer or IBM may terminate this Agreement for material breach of this Agreement by the other upon written notice containing the specific nature and dates of the material breach. The breaching party will have thirty (30) days from receipt of notice to cure such breach, except for nonpayment by Customer, which must be cured within seven (7) business days from receipt of notice. If such breach has not been timely cured, then the non-breaching party may immediately terminate this Agreement upon written notice; provided, however, it is understood that in the event IBM has so breached this Agreement IBM shall not be entitled to recover the early termination charges described in Section 3.4(b) below.

Rule:
ID: LICENSE
Title: Licence grant scope
Kind: parametric
Summary: The licence must cover our affiliates and contractors and must not be revocable at will.
Severity: high
Category: licence
Position — preferred:
Licence extends to Customer's affiliates and to contractors acting on Customer's behalf; paid-up licences are perpetual and irrevocable; subscription licences terminable only for uncured material breach; transferable to successors.

Position — fallback:
Affiliates covered on written notice; transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction.
Position — walk-away:
Licence revocable at Vendor's discretion; affiliates and contractors excluded with no path to add them.
Detection guidance:
Find the grant clause: "non-exclusive, non-transferable", "revocable", "solely for Customer's internal use", whether affiliates/contractors are named, term of the licence.

Redline guidance:
Insert "and its Affiliates and contractors acting on its behalf", delete "revocable", add successor transfer.

Unlimited or unannounced audits, or remote access to Customer systems.

Find audit/inspection/verification rights binding Customer; extract frequency, notice, cost allocation, system access.

Insert the frequency/notice/cost limits with minimal edits; delete system-access language.

Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc.; counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation.

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc.; counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation.

Rule:
ID: LD
Title: Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer
Kind: direction
Summary: Service credits to us are welcome; liquidated damages against us are not.
Severity: high
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer.
Position — fallback:
Early-termination fee capped at 3 months' fees as the sole liquidated amount.
Position — walk-away:
Liquidated damages exceeding the remaining contract value or triggered by minor breaches.
Detection guidance:
Identify liquidated damages, penalties, minimum fees on termination, "shall pay … as liquidated damages". Flag only when Customer pays. Service credits or LDs payable by Vendor to Customer are compliant.

Redline guidance:
Delete the Customer-payable LD; if an early-termination fee is unavoidable, cap it at 3 months' fees.

Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc.; counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation.

Rule:
ID: MINCOMMIT
Title: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not take-or-pay without an exit.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No minimum commitment; fees are for usage or ordered services only.
Position — fallback:
Commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.
Position — walk-away:
Multi-year take-or-pay commitments with no reduction or termination right.
Detection guidance:
"minimum", "commit to purchase", "take or pay", "shortfall", volume caps on Customer usage. Commitments the Vendor makes to us are fine.
Redline guidance:
Delete or narrow to the fallback with minimal edits; replace shortfall penalties with a true-up.

input.summary: Insert a new § 14.12A requiring IBM to carry CGL, E&O, cyber and workers' compensation insurance with certificates on request.
input.comment: [Playbook] The Agreement has no insurance requirement even though IBM hosts our environment and processes data on our behalf, so we have added a standard clause (CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M, statutory workers' compensation, certificates on request) immediately after Risk of Loss. If these limits are an issue we can accept E&O of USD 1M and cyber of USD 2M.

ops.text: Insurance

IBM shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term of this Agreement and for one (1) year thereafter: (a) commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; (b) professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; (c) cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000 covering the Services and any Customer Components, Content or personal information processed by IBM on Customer's behalf; and (d) workers' compensation insurance as required by applicable law. IBM shall provide certificates of insurance to Customer on request.

Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc.; counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation.

Rule:
ID: INSURANCE
Title: Vendor insurance
Kind: missing
Summary: Vendors that touch our data or premises carry standard insurance.
Severity: low
Category: insurance
Position — preferred:
Commercial general liability USD 1M per occurrence / 2M aggregate; professional (E&O) USD 2M; cyber/privacy USD 5M for vendors processing Customer Data; workers' compensation as required by law; certificates on request.

Position — fallback:
E&O USD 1M and cyber USD 2M.
Position — walk-away:
No insurance for a vendor that processes personal data or works on our premises.
Detection guidance:
Look for an insurance clause; if absent for a services/hosting vendor, deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a short insurance paragraph in the general/miscellaneous section.
Model language:
Vendor shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term and for one (1) year thereafter: commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; and, where Vendor processes Customer Data, cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000. Vendor shall provide certificates of insurance on request.

ops.text: Insurance

IBM shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term of this Agreement and for one (1) year thereafter: (a) commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; (b) professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; (c) cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000 covering the Services and any Customer Components, Content or personal information processed by IBM on Customer's behalf; and (d) workers' compensation insurance as required by applicable law. Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc.; counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation.

Rule:
ID: LICENSE
Title: Licence grant scope
Kind: parametric
Summary: The licence must cover our affiliates and contractors and must not be revocable at will.
Severity: high
Category: licence
Position — preferred:
Licence extends to Customer's affiliates and to contractors acting on Customer's behalf; paid-up licences are perpetual and irrevocable; subscription licences terminable only for uncured material breach; transferable to successors.

Position — fallback:
Affiliates covered on written notice; transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction.
Position — walk-away:
Licence revocable at Vendor's discretion; affiliates and contractors excluded with no path to add them.
Detection guidance:
Find the grant clause: "non-exclusive, non-transferable", "revocable", "solely for Customer's internal use", whether affiliates/contractors are named, term of the licence.

Redline guidance:
Insert "and its Affiliates and contractors acting on its behalf", delete "revocable", add successor transfer.

input.rationale: Section 3.4(b) conditions our convenience-termination right on paying "early termination charges" of unspecified amount, set out in Attachment A and Service Option Attachments (which IBM may unilaterally amend under Section 13.1). We proposed deleting the charge, with a fallback cap of three months' recurring charges if an early-termination fee is unavoidable.

content.text:
**Finding: Deviation (medium)** — WARRANTY

- **What the document says:** § 5.1 warrants only that IBM will perform Services "using reasonable care and skill" and that it has corporate authority, plus a covenant to comply with laws applicable to IBM's own business. § 5.2 makes those the exclusive warranties, and § 5.4(c) provides all Materials and non-IBM items "AS IS, WITHOUT WARRANTY OF ANY KIND."
- **Gap vs. playbook:** no conformance-to-documentation warranty for Deliverables/Materials, no no-malicious-code warranty, and no remedy (repair, replacement, re-performance or refund). The broad "AS IS" language would also swallow any conformance protection.
- **Redline (validated, preferred level):** inserted a new § 5.1(c) with a 90-day conformance and malicious-code warranty and an express repair/replace/re-perform/refund remedy (at IBM's option), and prefaced § 5.4(c) with "EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY WARRANTED IN SECTION 5.1" to preserve the express warranty.
- **Fallback flagged in the comment:** a shorter warranty period is negotiable provided the remedy stands.

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.


Claimed finding status: deviation

Finding rationale:
Section 5.1 gives only a care-and-skill warranty for Services plus authority and a law-compliance covenant; there is no conformance warranty for Deliverables/Materials, no no-malicious-code warranty and no stated remedy (repair, replacement, re-performance or refund). Section 5.4(c) then provides all Materials "AS IS" without warranty of any kind, which swallows any conformance protection, and 5.2 makes 5.1 exclusive. This falls short of the preferred position, so we add a 90-day conformance and malicious-code warranty with an express remedy and carve the Section 5.1 warranties out of the "AS IS" disclaimer.

Original paragraphs:
p0061: a. it will perform the Services using reasonable care and skill and in accordance with the applicable Service Option Attachments (which means the degree of knowledge, skill and judgment customarily exercised by members of the applicable profession with respect to work of a similar nature); and that it will provide Customer with competent, fully trained, fully qualified and responsible personnel to perform the Services; and
p0062: b. it has the requisite corporate power and authority to execute, deliver and perform its obligations under this Agreement.
p0065: THE WARRANTIES IN SECTION 5.1 ARE THE EXCLUSIVE WARRANTIES FROM IBM. THEY REPLACE ALL OTHER WARRANTIES, INCLUDING, WITHOUT LIMITATION, THE IMPLIED WARRANTIES OF MERCHANTABILITY, SATISFACTORY QUALITY, AND FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE.
p0074: c. IBM PROVIDES ALL MATERIALS AND ALL NON-IBM SERVICES, PRODUCTS, DATA, APPARATUS AND SOFTWARE "AS IS", WITHOUT WARRANTY OF ANY KIND, INCLUDING, WITHOUT LIMITATION, THE IMPLIED WARRANTIES OF MERCHANTABILITY, SATISFACTORY QUALITY, AND FITNESS FOR&sbsp;A PARTICULAR PURPOSE. Non-IBM suppliers may provide their own warranties to you.

Resolved definitions:
Customer: Under this e-business Hosting Agreement ("Agreement") between International Business Machines Corporation ("IBM") and Bluefly, Inc. ("Customer"), IBM will provide Web hosting and related services ("Services") to Customer. The Agreement includes these terms and conditions and the documents referenced herein ("Base Terms"), e-business hosting services order forms accepted by IBM ("Order Forms"), and the following attachments:
Service Option Attachments: c. all other applicable attachments referenced in the Order Forms for Services options selected by Customer ("Service Option Attachments").

Rendered redline:
p0062: b. it has the requisite corporate power and authority to execute, deliver and perform its obligations under this Agreement.
c. for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable and all Materials delivered by IBM will conform in all material respects to their applicable documentation and specifications, and will not contain any virus, malicious or disabling code. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at IBM's option, re-performance of the non-conforming Services, repair or replacement of the non-conforming Deliverable or Materials, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services, Deliverable or Materials.
p0074: c. EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY WARRANTED IN SECTION 5.1, IBM PROVIDES ALL MATERIALS AND ALL NON-IBM SERVICES, PRODUCTS, DATA, APPARATUS AND SOFTWARE "AS IS", WITHOUT WARRANTY OF ANY KIND, INCLUDING, WITHOUT LIMITATION, THE IMPLIED WARRANTIES OF MERCHANTABILITY, SATISFACTORY QUALITY, AND FITNESS FOR&sbsp;A PARTICULAR PURPOSE. Non-IBM suppliers may provide their own warranties to you.

Comment:
[Playbook] We have added a 90-day conformance warranty for delivered Materials, a no-malicious-code warranty and an express repair/re-performance/refund remedy, since Section 5.1 currently gives us no conformance warranty or remedy at all. We have also carved the Section 5.1 warranties out of the Section 5.4(c) "AS IS" disclaimer so that the disclaimer does not swallow the express warranty; we can discuss a shorter period if IBM prefers.

input.quote: IBM grants Customer a nonexclusive, revocable license to use the Base Components solely in connection with the Services as provided under this Agreement.
input.rationale: The § 12.1 grant is expressly "revocable", so IBM could withdraw the Base Components licence at will, and it names only "Customer" — it does not extend to our Affiliates (defined at p0015) or to our Subcontractors (defined at p0031), even though Content Administrators and Services Recipients are expected to include Subcontractors and other entities. Nothing else cures this: § 14.17 confirms only expressly stated licences are granted, and § 14.10 permits assignment of the Agreement to a successor but does not make the licence itself transferable. This falls short of the preferred position (affiliates/contractors covered, no at-will revocation, terminable only for uncured material breach, transferable to successors) and close to the walk-away. Redline extends the grant to Affiliates and Subcontractors acting on our behalf, deletes "revocable" and "solely", makes the licence irrevocable during the term subject to termination for uncured material breach under § 3.3, and confirms transfer to a successor under a permitted § 14.10 assignment.

proposal.summary: Extend Base Components licence to Customer Affiliates and Subcontractors, remove "revocable", and confirm irrevocability during term plus successor transfer.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have extended the Base Components licence to our Affiliates and to Subcontractors acting on our behalf, deleted "revocable" so the licence cannot be pulled at will, and confirmed it runs for the term (subject only to termination for uncured material breach under Section 3.3) and passes to a successor under a permitted assignment. Our licence position does not accept a discretionary revocation right or a grant that excludes the affiliates and contractors who actually use the Services; if helpful, we can accept Affiliate coverage on written notice as a fallback.

input.quote: IBM grants Customer a nonexclusive, revocable license to use the Base Components solely in connection with the Services as provided under this Agreement.
input.rationale: The § 12.1 grant is expressly "revocable", so IBM could withdraw the Base Components licence at will, and it names only "Customer" — it does not extend to our Affiliates (defined at p0015) or to our Subcontractors (defined at p0031), even though Content Administrators and Services Recipients are expected to include Subcontractors and other entities. Nothing else cures this: § 14.17 confirms only expressly stated licences are granted, and § 14.10 permits assignment of the Agreement to a successor but does not make the licence itself transferable. This falls short of the preferred position (affiliates/contractors covered, no at-will revocation, terminable only for uncured material breach, transferable to successors) and close to the walk-away. Redline extends the grant to Affiliates and Subcontractors acting on our behalf, deletes "revocable" and "solely", makes the licence irrevocable during the term subject to termination for uncured material breach under § 3.3, and confirms transfer to a successor under a permitted § 14.10 assignment.

**Finding: deviation (high severity, LD rule)**

- **Where:** § 3.4(b) Termination for Convenience (p0046), cross-referenced in § 3.3 (p0042).
- **Issue:** Our convenience-termination right is conditioned on paying unquantified "early termination charges" specified in Attachment A and Service Option Attachments — a Customer-payable liquidated amount with no cap, made worse by § 13.1 letting IBM unilaterally change Attachment A terms on notice.
- **Checked and clear:** § 4.2 refers only to late payment fees; § 9.2 limits Customer liability to actual direct damages; no other Customer-payable penalty or minimum-fee mechanic appears (no "liquidated damages" language anywhere in the document).
- **Redline (validated, preferred):** replaces 3.4(b) so we pay only charges accrued through the termination date and expressly owe no early termination charge, penalty, liquidated damages, or unearned minimum; the comment offers the fallback of a charge capped at three months' recurring charges if IBM insists.

Rule:
ID: LD
Title: Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer
Kind: direction
Summary: Service credits to us are welcome; liquidated damages against us are not.
Severity: high
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer.
Position — fallback:
Early-termination fee capped at 3 months' fees as the sole liquidated amount.
Position — walk-away:
Liquidated damages exceeding the remaining contract value or triggered by minor breaches.
Detection guidance:
Identify liquidated damages, penalties, minimum fees on termination, "shall pay … as liquidated damages". Flag only when Customer pays. Service credits or LDs payable by Vendor to Customer are compliant.

Redline guidance:
Delete the Customer-payable LD; if an early-termination fee is unavoidable, cap it at 3 months' fees.

Claimed finding status: deviation

Finding rationale:
Section 3.4(b) conditions our convenience-termination right on paying "early termination charges" of unspecified amount, set out in Attachment A and Service Option Attachments (which IBM may unilaterally amend under Section 13.1). That is a liquidated amount payable by the Customer with no cap, contrary to the preferred position of no liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer; Section 3.3 confirms these charges are otherwise payable except where IBM has breached. No Customer-payable liquidated damages appear elsewhere (Section 4.2 refers only to late payment fees, and Section 9.2 caps Customer liability to actual direct damages). We proposed deleting the charge, with a fallback cap of three months' recurring charges if an early-termination fee is unavoidable.

Original paragraphs:
p0046: b. paying the applicable early termination charges, if any, specified in Attachment A and applicable Service Option Attachments.
p0042: Customer or IBM may terminate this Agreement for material breach of this Agreement by the other upon written notice containing the specific nature and dates of the material breach. The breaching party will have thirty (30) days from receipt of notice to cure such breach, except for nonpayment by Customer, which must be cured within seven (7) business days from receipt of notice. If such breach has not been timely cured, then the non-breaching party may immediately terminate this Agreement upon written notice; provided, however, it is understood that in the event IBM has so breached this Agreement IBM shall not be entitled to recover the early termination charges described in Section 3.4(b) below.

Resolved definitions:
Customer: Under this e-business Hosting Agreement ("Agreement") between International Business Machines Corporation ("IBM") and Bluefly, Inc. ("Customer"), IBM will provide Web hosting and related services ("Services") to Customer. The Agreement includes these terms and conditions and the documents referenced herein ("Base Terms"), e-business hosting services order forms accepted by IBM ("Order Forms"), and the following attachments:
Service Option Attachments: c. all other applicable attachments referenced in the Order Forms for Services options selected by Customer ("Service Option Attachments").

Rendered redline:
p0046: b. paying all charges accrued for Services performed through the effective date of termination. Customer will not be liable for any early termination charge, penalty, liquidated damages, or other minimum or unearned amount in respect of such termination.

Comment:
[Playbook] We have removed the open-ended early termination charges payable by us on convenience termination, since our playbook does not permit liquidated damages or penalties payable by the Customer, particularly where the amount sits in Attachment A that IBM may change unilaterally under Section 13.1. If an early termination charge is essential, we can accept one capped at three months' recurring charges for the terminated Services as the sole such amount.

input.quote: IBM reserves the right to investigate potential violations of the representations and warranties in Subsection 11.2(b).
input.rationale: § 11.3 is the only inspection/verification right binding Customer, and it is unqualified: IBM may investigate potential AUP breaches at any frequency, without prior notice (p0137 only requires attempted notice before restricting access or removing Content), with no limits on access to Customer systems, no independent-auditor or confidentiality requirement, and no cost allocation, while p0138 obliges Customer to hand over all relevant information on request. That sits at the playbook walk-away position (unlimited/unannounced investigation with potential system access), so we inserted the standard guardrails: once per 12 months, 30 days' written notice, business hours, independent auditor under confidentiality, off-site where practicable with no direct system access, and IBM's cost unless an underpayment exceeds 5%.

proposal.summary: Add frequency, notice, business-hours, independent-auditor, cost and no-system-access limits to IBM's investigation right in § 11.3.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] IBM's investigation right in 11.3 is currently unlimited, unannounced and at our cost, so we have added our standard audit guardrails: once per 12 months, 30 days' written notice, business hours, an independent auditor under confidentiality, off-site review where practicable with no direct access to our systems, and IBM's cost unless an underpayment exceeds 5%. We can fall back to 15 days' notice and a 10% underpayment threshold if needed.

ops.text: Any investigation under this Subsection 11.3 that requires access to Customer's records, facilities or systems will be conducted: (i) no more than once in any twelve (12) month period; (ii) upon at least thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Customer; (iii) during Customer's normal business hours and in a manner that does not unreasonably disrupt Customer's business; (iv) by an independent third-party auditor bound by written confidentiality obligations no less protective than those of this Agreement; (v) remotely or off-site wherever practicable, and IBM will have no direct access to Customer systems or Customer Components; and (vi) at IBM's expense, unless the investigation reveals an underpayment by Customer exceeding five percent (5%) of the amounts due for the period reviewed, in which case Customer will reimburse IBM's reasonable costs of the investigation.

That sits at the playbook walk-away position (unlimited/unannounced investigation with potential system access), so we inserted the standard guardrails: once per 12 months, 30 days' written notice, business hours, independent auditor under confidentiality, off-site where practicable with no direct system access, and IBM's cost unless an underpayment exceeds 5%.

proposal.summary: Add frequency, notice, business-hours, independent-auditor, cost and no-system-access limits to IBM's investigation right in § 11.3.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] IBM's investigation right in 11.3 is currently unlimited, unannounced and at our cost, so we have added our standard audit guardrails: once per 12 months, 30 days' written notice, business hours, an independent auditor under confidentiality, off-site review where practicable with no direct access to our systems, and IBM's cost unless an underpayment exceeds 5%. We can fall back to 15 days' notice and a 10% underpayment threshold if needed.

ops.text: Any investigation under this Subsection 11.3 that requires access to Customer's records, facilities or systems will be conducted: (i) no more than once in any twelve (12) month period; (ii) upon at least thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Customer; (iii) during Customer's normal business hours and in a manner that does not unreasonably disrupt Customer's business; (iv) by an independent third-party auditor bound by written confidentiality obligations no less protective than those of this Agreement; (v) remotely or off-site wherever practicable, and IBM will have no direct access to Customer systems or Customer Components; and (vi) at IBM's expense, unless the investigation reveals an underpayment by Customer exceeding five percent (5%) of the amounts due for the period reviewed, in which case Customer will reimburse IBM's reasonable costs of the investigation.

Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc.; counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation.

Rule:
ID: AUDIT
Title: Audit rights against Customer
Kind: parametric
Summary: Audits of our usage must be rare, notified, off-site where possible and at the Vendor's cost.
Severity: medium
Category: audit
Position — preferred:
No more than once per 12 months, on 30 days' written notice, during business hours, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, at Vendor's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5 %; no direct access to Customer systems.

Position — fallback:
Once per year on 15 days' notice; Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 10 %.
Position — walk-away:
Unlimited or unannounced audits, or remote access to Customer systems.
Detection guidance:
Find audit/inspection/verification rights binding Customer; extract frequency, notice, cost allocation, system access.
Redline guidance:
Insert the frequency/notice/cost limits with minimal edits; delete system-access language.

Rule:
ID: MINCOMMIT
Title: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not take-or-pay without an exit.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No minimum commitment; fees are for usage or ordered services only.
Position — fallback:
Commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.
Position — walk-away:
Multi-year take-or-pay commitments with no reduction or termination right.
Detection guidance:
"minimum", "commit to purchase", "take or pay", "shortfall", volume caps on Customer usage. Commitments the Vendor makes to us are fine.
Redline guidance:
Delete or narrow to the fallback with minimal edits; replace shortfall penalties with a true-up.

**Finding: deviation (high severity) — § 12.1 License**

The grant is "nonexclusive, **revocable**" and runs to "Customer" only:

- **At-will revocation:** IBM can pull the Base Components licence at any time, independent of the termination machinery in § 3.3.

Fallback offered in the comment: Affiliate coverage on written notice.

paragraphs.text: 3.4 Termination for Convenience

Customer may terminate this Agreement (including all Service Option Attachments) or any Service Option Attachment (with the exception of any Service Option Attachment that is a prerequisite for the provision of Services under a non-terminated Service Option Attachment) for convenience at the end of any calendar month by:
a. providing at least one month's prior written notice to IBM; and
b. paying the applicable early termination charges, if any, specified in Attachment A and applicable Service Option Attachments.
In the event that Customer exercises its rights under this Section 3.4, IBM shall continue to fulfill all of its duties and obligations following the notice date and until the final termination date.
3.2 Renewal

Each Service Option Attachment will renew automatically for an additional term equal in duration to the previous term of the applicable Service Option Attachment unless either party notifies the other party in writing at least ninety (90) days prior to the end of the then-current term for the applicable Service Option Attachment that it has elected to terminate such Service Option Attachment.

paragraphs.text: 14.2 Survival

Any of these terms and conditions which by their nature extend beyond the Agreement termination or expiration remain in effect until fulfilled, including, without limitation, Sections 3.5, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11.2, 11.3, 11.6, 12.2, 12.3, and 14, and apply to both Customer's and IBM's respective successors and assignees.
14.18 Data Protection

You agree to allow International Business Machines Corporation and entities within its Enterprise to store and use your contact information, including names, phone numbers, and e-mail addresses, anywhere they do business. For personal information processed by IBM on your behalf as part of the Services, IBM will act in accordance with your instructions by following such processing and security obligations as are contained in this Agreement. You also confirm that you are solely responsible for ensuring that any processing and security obligations comply with applicable data protection laws. Your contact information shall not be considered personal information processed on your behalf.

reasons: Deviation is correctly identified: § 11.3 gives IBM an open-ended right to investigate Customer's use/Content with no frequency cap, no prior written notice (p0137 only requires an *attempted* notice, and only before 11.3(a)/(b) actions), no independent-auditor or confidentiality requirement, no limit on access to Customer records/systems and no cost allocation, with p0138 obliging Customer to hand over information on request — i.e. below the AUDIT preferred and fallback positions.

Redline is valid and minimal: a single appended paragraph after p0137 that leaves existing text untouched and delivers all preferred elements (once per 12 months, 30 days' written notice, business hours, independent auditor under confidentiality, off-site where practicable with no direct system access, Vendor cost unless >5% underpayment). Scoping it to investigations 'that require access to Customer's records, facilities or systems' is a sensible narrowing that avoids blocking IBM's ability to act on its own hosted environment.

Comment is accurate on substance, cites the playbook position and offers the 15-day/10% fallback in the required tone; the only slip is describing the current right as 'at our cost' when the original is simply silent on cost allocation — worth softening to 'with no cost allocation'.

Refinements for the drafter (not fatal): (i) consider preserving § 11.3's existing emergency / required-by-law carve-out as an exception to the 30-day notice, since a flat 30-day requirement for suspected illegal-content investigations is likely to be rejected outright; (ii) limb (vi) imports a fee-audit 'underpayment exceeding 5% of amounts due for the period reviewed' concept into an acceptable-use investigation clause — retain the 'at IBM's expense' default but confirm the underpayment trigger is coherent here so it does not invite IBM to recharacterise 11.3 as a payment audit.

Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc.; counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation.

Rule:
ID: MINCOMMIT
Title: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not take-or-pay without an exit.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No minimum commitment; fees are for usage or ordered services only.
Position — fallback:
Commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.
Position — walk-away:
Multi-year take-or-pay commitments with no reduction or termination right.
Detection guidance:
"minimum", "commit to purchase", "take or pay", "shortfall", volume caps on Customer usage. Commitments the Vendor makes to us are fine.
Redline guidance:
Delete or narrow to the fallback with minimal edits; replace shortfall penalties with a true-up.

Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc.; counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation.

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc.; counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation.

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

Rule:
ID: MINCOMMIT
Title: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not take-or-pay without an exit.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No minimum commitment; fees are for usage or ordered services only.
Position — fallback:
Commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.
Position — walk-away:
Multi-year take-or-pay commitments with no reduction or termination right.
Detection guidance:
"minimum", "commit to purchase", "take or pay", "shortfall", volume caps on Customer usage. Commitments the Vendor makes to us are fine.
Redline guidance:
Delete or narrow to the fallback with minimal edits; replace shortfall penalties with a true-up.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc.; counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation.

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc.; counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation.

Rule:
ID: MINCOMMIT
Title: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not take-or-pay without an exit.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No minimum commitment; fees are for usage or ordered services only.
Position — fallback:
Commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.
Position — walk-away:
Multi-year take-or-pay commitments with no reduction or termination right.
Detection guidance:
"minimum", "commit to purchase", "take or pay", "shortfall", volume caps on Customer usage. Commitments the Vendor makes to us are fine.
Redline guidance:
Delete or narrow to the fallback with minimal edits; replace shortfall penalties with a true-up.

input.rationale: § 3.5 (Effect of Termination) addresses only Customer's payment obligations; searches for transition, return, export and deletion language return nothing, and § 14.18 (Data Protection) and § 11.6 (Content) impose no exit obligations on IBM. In a hosting agreement where Customer's Content resides in IBM's e-business Hosting Environment, the absence of any transition-assistance, data-return or deletion-certification obligation is a deviation. Inserted the playbook exit provision into § 3.5, which already survives termination under § 14.2.

proposal.summary: Insert transition assistance, data return and deletion certification obligations into § 3.5 (Effect of Termination)
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have added an exit provision to § 3.5 so that, on expiry or termination, IBM provides up to six months of transition assistance at its then-current rates, returns our Content in a machine-readable format within 30 days, and then deletes it and certifies deletion; the Agreement is otherwise silent on getting our data back or migrating services. If six months is too long, we can accept 90 days of transition assistance with the same 30-day export and deletion certification.

ops.text: Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement or any Service Option Attachment for any reason, IBM shall: (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months following the effective date of termination at IBM's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days of Customer's request, return or make available to Customer for export all Content and other Customer data in IBM's possession or control, in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete such Content and Customer data from its systems and certify such deletion to Customer in writing.

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position. Use fallback only when the rule guidance or existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.

Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc.; counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation.

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

input.quote: b. paying the applicable early termination charges, if any, specified in Attachment A and applicable Service Option Attachments.
input.rationale: The Base Terms contain no express minimum purchase, volume or take-or-pay commitment (§ 4.1 charges are one-time, installment, recurring or usage-based, and § 3.5 limits Customer's liability on termination to accrued amounts). However, § 3.4(b) conditions Customer's termination-for-convenience right on payment of undefined "early termination charges" specified in Attachment A and Service Option Attachments, which — combined with automatic renewal for terms of equal duration under § 3.2 — creates an open-ended penalty for exiting and functions as take-or-pay exposure for Services never received. Per the playbook we narrowed the exit payment to a true-up of IBM's unavoidable direct costs and confirmed no minimum purchase or volume commitment, preserving the existing one-month exit right.

ops.oldText: b. paying the applicable early termination charges, if any, specified in Attachment A and applicable Service Option Attachments.
ops.newText: b. paying, in lieu of any early termination charge, penalty or minimum purchase or volume commitment, a true-up equal to IBM's actual, reasonable and documented direct costs attributable to the terminated Services that IBM cannot reasonably avoid or mitigate. Customer will have no obligation to pay for Services not rendered.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We do not take take-or-pay exposure, so we have replaced the open-ended early termination charges referenced to Attachment A with a true-up limited to IBM's unavoidable direct costs and confirmed there is no minimum purchase or volume commitment. If IBM needs term protection, we can accept a commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, provided any exit payment remains a true-up rather than a penalty.
proposal.summary: Convert Section 3.4(b) early termination charges into an unavoidable-cost true-up and confirm no minimum purchase or volume commitment.

Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc.; counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation.

Rule:
ID: MINCOMMIT
Title: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not take-or-pay without an exit.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No minimum commitment; fees are for usage or ordered services only.
Position — fallback:
Commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.
Position — walk-away:
Multi-year take-or-pay commitments with no reduction or termination right.
Detection guidance:
"minimum", "commit to purchase", "take or pay", "shortfall", volume caps on Customer usage. Commitments the Vendor makes to us are fine.
Redline guidance:
Delete or narrow to the fallback with minimal edits; replace shortfall penalties with a true-up.

content.text:
**Finding: missing (medium) — TRANSITION**

The agreement has no post-termination transition or data-return obligation:

- **§ 3.5 Effect of Termination** covers only Customer's accrued payment obligations.
- No hits anywhere for transition, data return/export, or deletion language.
- **§ 14.18 Data Protection** and **§ 11.6 Content** place responsibility on Customer and impose no exit duties on IBM — significant given Customer's "Content" sits in IBM's e-business Hosting Environment.

**Redline (validated, preferred position):** inserted a new paragraph after p0049 in § 3.5 requiring IBM to (a) provide up to six months of transition assistance at then-current rates, (b) return/export all Content in a commonly used machine-readable format within 30 days, and (c) thereafter delete and certify deletion in writing. § 3.5 is already enumerated in the § 14.2 survival list, so the new obligations survive termination without further amendment. Fallback offered in the comment: 90 days of transition assistance with the same 30-day export and deletion certification.
